# Document Review

Review a requirements or plan document with a team of reviewer personas. Dispatch generic subagents, each seeded with a skill-local reviewer prompt. Synthesis sorts the findings: apply and report the ones it routes to Apply, in the document's native format, and route the rest to the user.

**Done when:** every dispatched reviewer returned or was named as failed in Coverage, the fixes routed to Apply are applied and reported, and the rest went through the four-option interaction (interactive) or came back as structured text with classifications intact (non-interactive).


## Interactive mode rules

**Read `references/modes.md` before anything else.** It owns mode detection, the non-interactive argument contract, and the question-tool rules: match the host's blocking question tool already in the current tool list (never call a user-facing question tool to discover it), pre-load it at the top of the interactive flow if it is listed but unloaded, and fall back to a numbered list only when the harness genuinely lacks one.

Either way, a question that calls for a user decision fires the tool or falls back loudly. Narrating it as text is a bug.

## Artifact Root

Resolve `<root>` **only** in the no-path interactive branch, which discovers the most recent plan under `<root>/plans/`. Every other run reads the document at the path it was handed. So an absolute-path or non-interactive review — `/tmp/plan.md`, possibly outside any repo — never depends on a repo root or a CE config it does not need.

<!-- ce-docs-root:start -->
**Resolve the CE artifact root `<root>` before composing any artifact path.**

- **Read** `docs_root` from `<repo-root>/.compound-engineering/config.yaml` only (`<repo-root>` = `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`). Do not read it from `config.local.yaml`. Unset -> `<root>` is `docs`, exactly as before.
- **Validate** a set value: a repo-relative directory whose real, symlink-resolved path stays inside the repo and is neither the repo root nor under `.git/`. Otherwise stop with an error naming `docs_root` and the value -- never fall back to `docs`.
- **Use** `<root>` as the sole artifact location: create it if absent, compose each path as `<root>/<subdir>` with this skill's own subdirectory, and never also read `docs`.
<!-- ce-docs-root:end -->

## Phase 1: Get and Analyze Document

**Read `references/document-intake.md` now.** It covers how the document is obtained in each mode, the missing-document gate and its failure text, and the classification signals.

Two of its rules bound every later step.

**Verify before any dispatch.** Every resolved path must be readable on disk. If one is not, dispatch **no** personas: reviewers read from the filesystem, so they cannot reach a path that exists only on an unchecked-out branch (issue #925).

**Classify by content shape and metadata, not by file path.** `artifact_readiness: requirements-only` is a **`unified-requirements`** review — Product Contract only. A missing Planning Contract, Implementation Unit, Verification Contract, or Definition of Done is expected there, never a finding. `artifact_readiness: implementation-ready` is a **`unified-plan`**. Anything else takes the legacy `requirements` / `plan` split.

HTML unified artifacts take the same routes. Every fix lands in the document's native format; never insert markdown into HTML. That reference covers ID-bearing items. Pass the classification to each persona in the `{document_type}` slot.

## Phase 2: Announce and Dispatch Personas

**Read `references/persona-selection.md`** for each conditional persona's activation signals and the announcement format. Two of those signals over-activate on plausible evidence: the sensitive-data bound on `security-lens-reviewer`, and the challenge-surface bar on `adversarial-document-reviewer`. Then read **`references/dispatch.md`** for payload variables, slicing, model tiering, and reviewer-failure handling.

The team is `coherence-reviewer` and `feasibility-reviewer` always, plus each activated conditional persona. Announce the team with a per-persona justification before any dispatch.

Dispatch generic subagents with **bounded parallelism** through the platform's subagent primitive. Seed each one with the full content of its `references/personas/<reviewer-name>.md`. Never dispatch a standalone agent by type or name.

A capacity rejection is backpressure, not reviewer failure. That reviewer stays queued and retries when a slot frees, and no reviewer is dropped because the harness cap is below the team size.

### Cross-Model Judgment Pass

Run this pass if any of the **conditional judgment trio** was activated: `adversarial-document-reviewer`, `product-lens-reviewer`, `security-lens-reviewer`. Follow `references/cross-model-review.md`, which owns the pass end to end: host attestation, the one target and route used for the whole document, the disclosure before any egress, and how peers are launched, reaped, and folded in.

The pass is additive and non-blocking: a failure or timeout stops nothing and is named in Coverage. The checkout egress policy (`cross_model_review_mode`) is evaluated first and can skip the pass with a named reason. Filter recipients only when `CROSS_MODEL_PEERS` is set — unset means unfiltered, not unsanctioned. Never silently change an explicit model or recipient.

## Phases 3-5: Synthesis, Presentation, and Next Action

Wait until every dispatched agent has returned, including any cross-model `<reviewer-name>-<provider>.json` returns. Then read `references/synthesis-and-presentation.md`. It owns the synthesis pipeline, the routing of each finding by confidence and fix class, fix application, the non-interactive envelope, and the handoff to the routing question. When promoting agreement, only an artifact with `independence_verified: true` counts as an independent reviewer.

**Interactive mode only.** Read `references/walkthrough.md` for the grouped confirmation, the routing question, and the per-finding walk-through. Read `references/bulk-preview.md` for the bulk-action preview behind best-judgment routing, Append-to-Open-Questions, and auto-resolve. Load neither before dispatch completes, and a non-interactive run never loads them at all — it stops at the synthesis envelope.

# Mode detection and the interactive question tool

## Interactive mode rules

- **Pre-load the host's blocking question tool already in the current tool list before any question fires.** If the matching tool is listed but unloaded, use the host's tool-discovery primitive once at the start of the Interactive flow to load that capability — do not search for another host's tool name. Presence in the current tool list is proof; never call a user-facing question tool to discover whether it exists. The grouped confirmation, routing question, per-finding walk-through, bulk-preview Proceed/Cancel, and the Phase 5 terminal question all depend on it.
- **The numbered-list fallback applies only when the harness genuinely lacks a blocking question tool** — no matching tool is in the current list, a real question call errors, or the runtime mode does not expose one. In genuine-fallback cases, present options as a numbered list on the host's user-visible chat surface and wait for the reply. A question that calls for a user decision must either fire the tool or fall back loudly — rendering it as narrative text because the tool feels inconvenient, because the model is in report-formatting mode, or because the instruction was buried in a long skill is a bug.

## Phase 0: Detect Mode

Arguments may contain a document path, a mode token, or both; both tokens together is not a conflict. Tokens starting with `mode:` are flags, not paths — strip them, and use any remaining token as the document path for Phase 1.

`mode:non-interactive` (or its deprecated alias `mode:headless`) sets **non-interactive mode**, which changes the delivery of the findings that were not applied, not the classification boundaries — apply the same judgment about which tier each finding belongs in:

- fixes synthesis routes to Apply are applied and reported in the change list (same as interactive)
- everything else — the grouped confirmation, decisions, and FYI observations — is returned as structured text with the original classifications intact, for the caller to handle — no blocking-question prompts, no interactive routing
- Phase 5 returns immediately with "Review complete" (no routing question, no terminal question)

**Non-interactive argument contract:** `mode:non-interactive <document-path>`, for example `mode:non-interactive <path-to-doc>.{md,html}`. `mode:headless` is a deprecated alias for the same contract.

Absent either token, run interactive, with the routing question, walk-through, and bulk-preview behaviors documented in `references/walkthrough.md` and `references/bulk-preview.md`.
# Getting the document, and classifying it

- **Path provided:** read it, then proceed. If the read fails or the file is not on disk, apply the missing-document gate below instead of continuing.
- **No path, interactive:** ask which document to review, or find the most recent under `<root>/plans/` with a file-search/glob tool.
- **No path, non-interactive:** output "Review failed: non-interactive mode requires a document path. Expected arguments: mode:non-interactive <path>" and stop without dispatching reviewers.

**Missing-document gate — verify before any dispatch.** Persona reviewers read from the filesystem and several run without Bash, so they cannot read git refs: a path that exists only on an unchecked-out branch wastes the entire persona team discovering they cannot proceed (issue #925). Confirm every resolved path is readable on disk before Phase 2. Location does not matter — an absolute path outside the checkout or a doc in another checkout reviews fine. If any path is unreadable, dispatch **no** personas:

- **Interactive:** stop and name the missing path(s): "Document(s) not found on disk: <paths>. Check out the branch containing them, use a worktree, or provide corrected readable paths before retrying the review."
- **Non-interactive:** output "Review failed: document(s) not found on disk: <paths>. Expected input: paths to readable files on disk; check out the branch containing them or provide corrected paths." and return without dispatching reviewers.

### Classify Document Type

Classify by **content shape and metadata, not file path** — under the unified plan contract a requirements-only and an implementation-ready plan both live in `<root>/plans/`, so location no longer signals type. Reviewers operate differently per classification, so a misclassification produces noisy or under-scrutinized findings.

First check the unified artifact contract (`artifact_contract: ce-unified-plan/v1`):

- `artifact_readiness: requirements-only` -> **`unified-requirements`**. Review the Product Contract only; the absence of Planning Contract, Implementation Units, Verification Contract, or Definition of Done is expected and must not be flagged.
- `artifact_readiness: implementation-ready` -> **`unified-plan`**. Review Product Contract and Planning Contract with different lenses, then Implementation Units/Verification/DoD for execution completeness.
- Progress-like readiness values (`active`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `done`) are invalid — a document-contract finding, not an execution state to honor.
- HTML unified artifacts (`.html`) use the same review and mutation routes. Apply changes in the document's native format and preserve its existing structure; never insert markdown syntax into HTML. For an ID-bearing HTML item, mirror the nearest sibling's structure and preserve both its anchor convention and visible ID text.

Otherwise decide between the two legacy types on these signals:

- **`requirements`** (what-to-build): frontmatter like `actors:`, `flows:`, `acceptance_examples:`, or brainstorm-shaped `status:`; headings such as `Acceptance Examples`, `Actors`, `Key Flows`, `User Flows`, `Outstanding Questions`, `Resolve Before Planning`; `R1`/`A1`/`F1`/`AE1` identifiers; framing on user/business problem, behavior, scope boundaries, success criteria; no implementation units, per-unit file lists, or unit-attached test scenarios.
- **`plan`** (how-to-build): frontmatter like `type: feat|fix|refactor`, `origin: docs/brainstorms/...`, or `product_contract_source: ce-brainstorm|ce-plan-bootstrap|legacy-requirements`; headings such as `Implementation Units`, `Output Structure`, `Key Technical Decisions`, `Risks & Dependencies`, `System-Wide Impact`; `U1`/`U2` unit identifiers; per-unit `Goal`/`Files`/`Approach`/`Test scenarios`/`Verification` fields; repo-relative paths to create/modify/test; framing on technical decisions, sequencing, implementer-facing detail.

**Tie-breaker:** treat the dominant content shape as authoritative; if shape is genuinely ambiguous, default to `requirements` (the conservative choice — it activates fewer plan-specific feasibility checks). Path location never disambiguates; a legacy `origin: docs/brainstorms/...` field still reads as a `plan` signal.

Pass the result to each persona via the `{document_type}` slot — personas adapt their analysis to it.

## Extract once, here, for the dispatch payload

Personas never re-parse the document for these, so Phase 1 extracts both and hands them down:

- `{origin_path}` — upstream Product Contract provenance: the document's `origin:` frontmatter when present, else `product_contract_source:<value>` when present, else `none`.
- `{settled_ktds}` — any Key Technical Decision **or Product Contract Key Decision** carrying a `session-settled:` annotation, listed as decision name, class (`user-directed` / `user-approved`), and rejected alternative; else the literal `none`.

An unfilled slot silently disables the provenance-gated technique suppression in product-lens, adversarial, and scope-guardian, so pass both even when the value is `none`.

# Selecting the review team

The team is `coherence-reviewer` and `feasibility-reviewer` always, plus each conditional persona whose signals the document shows.

Activate a conditional persona when the document shows its signals:

**product-lens** — the document stakes a product position — what to build, why, or what comes first — that a knowledgeable stakeholder could reasonably challenge and that no upstream Product Contract settled, or the work carries strategic weight beyond the immediate problem. Users may be end users, developers, operators, maintainers, or any other audience; the criteria are domain-agnostic. Either leg qualifies:

- *Unsettled product position* — a problem framing, a goal predicting a specific user outcome, or a prioritization that ranks what gets built against what is deferred, which the document's origin did not already settle. A choice among mechanisms for an agreed outcome is an implementation decision, not a product position; describing a task or restating known requirements stakes nothing.
- *Strategic weight* — the work could affect trajectory, perception, or positioning even with a sound premise: it shapes what the system becomes known for; it is a complexity or simplicity bet affecting adoption, onboarding, or cognitive load; it opens or closes future directions (path dependencies, architectural commitments); it carries opportunity cost — building this means not building something else.

**design-lens** — UI/UX references, frontend components, or visual design language; user flows, wireframes, screen/page/view mentions; interaction descriptions (forms, buttons, navigation, modals); responsive behavior or accessibility.

**security-lens** — auth/authorization, login flows, session management; API endpoints exposed to external clients; handling of **sensitive** data — PII, payments, tokens, credentials, secrets, encryption; third-party integrations with trust-boundary implications. Ordinary data handling is not a trigger, and neither is storage-layer churn on its own: an internal schema migration, field rename, or data-store move activates this lens only when the data is sensitive or the change alters who can read or write it. Deployment-ordering risk is a feasibility concern, not a security signal.

**scope-guardian** — multiple priority tiers (P0/P1/P2, must/should/nice-to-have); >8 distinct requirements or implementation units; stretch goals, nice-to-haves, or "future work" sections; scope boundary language misaligned with stated goals; goals that don't clearly connect to requirements.

**adversarial** — a high-value challenge surface, not merely structural complexity. Activate when ANY holds:

- A **requirements document** with 2+ challengeable claims (problem framing, solution selection, prioritization, predicted outcomes) — premise scrutiny is core to the brainstorm phase
- A **high-stakes domain** — auth, payments, billing, data migrations, privacy/compliance, external integrations, cryptography — regardless of doc type or size
- A **new abstraction, framework, or significant architectural pattern**, regardless of doc type
- A **plan with no validated upstream Product Contract signal** (no legacy `origin:` requirements doc and no `product_contract_source: ce-brainstorm` or `legacy-requirements`) — the premise wasn't validated upstream
- A **plan that explicitly extends scope** beyond its origin requirements doc (new actors, new flows, deferred-then-restored features)
- An **explicit alternatives section** or unresolved tradeoffs — adversarial helps stress-test the chosen direction

Do NOT activate adversarial on a routine plan that derives from a validated upstream Product Contract, stays in scope, and introduces no high-stakes domain or new abstraction. Validated provenance includes legacy `origin: docs/brainstorms/...`, `product_contract_source: ce-brainstorm`, and `product_contract_source: legacy-requirements`; a direct `product_contract_source: ce-plan-bootstrap` plan is greenfield and does not suppress premise-level techniques by itself. A well-structured plan with stated rationale is the plan doing its job, not adversarial signal — activating on that alone re-litigates settled questions.

## Announce the review team

Tell the user which personas will review and why, with a justification for each conditional one:

```
Reviewing with:
- coherence-reviewer (always-on)
- feasibility-reviewer (always-on)
- scope-guardian-reviewer -- plan has 12 requirements across 3 priority levels
- security-lens-reviewer -- plan adds API endpoints with auth flow
```

The team is `coherence-reviewer` and `feasibility-reviewer` always, plus each activated conditional persona (`product-lens-reviewer`, `design-lens-reviewer`, `security-lens-reviewer`, `scope-guardian-reviewer`, `adversarial-document-reviewer`).
# Dispatching the reviewers

Dispatch generic subagents with **bounded parallelism** using the platform's subagent primitive (e.g., `Agent` in Claude Code, `spawn_agent` in Codex) where available; otherwise run the work inline or serially. Omit the `mode` parameter so the user's configured permission settings apply. Respect the harness's active-subagent limit even at the 7-agent maximum: queue the selected reviewers, dispatch only as many as the harness accepts, and fill freed slots as reviewers complete. Treat active-agent/thread/concurrency-limit spawn errors as backpressure, not reviewer failure — leave the reviewer queued and retry after a slot frees, and if the harness cap is lower than the team size, queue the remainder rather than dropping it. Record a reviewer as failed only after a successful dispatch times out or fails, or when dispatch fails for a non-capacity reason that survives correcting the invocation.

For each selected reviewer, read `references/personas/<reviewer-name>.md` and pass its full content as `{persona_file}`. Do not dispatch standalone agents by type/name and do not rely on platform-level custom-agent registration.

**Model tiering lives here, not in prompt assets.** Local prompt files have no frontmatter and carry no model metadata. Apply these dispatch-time preferences when the platform exposes a known model override; otherwise omit the override and inherit the parent model rather than guessing a platform-specific model name:

- `coherence-reviewer`: cheapest capable extraction/reasoning tier.
- `security-lens-reviewer`, `feasibility-reviewer`, `product-lens-reviewer`, `adversarial-document-reviewer`: inherit the parent model unless the harness has an established high-capability review tier.
- `design-lens-reviewer`, `scope-guardian-reviewer`: platform mid-tier model.

Each subagent receives the prompt built from the subagent template included below, with these variables filled:

| Variable | Value |
|----------|-------|
| `{persona_file}` | Full content of the selected local prompt asset from `references/personas/` |
| `{schema}` | Content of the findings schema included below |
| `{document_type}` | "requirements", "plan", "unified-requirements", or "unified-plan" from Phase 1 classification |
| `{document_path}` | Path to the document |
| `{origin_path}` | Upstream Product Contract provenance extracted once during Phase 1: prefer the document's `origin:` frontmatter field when present; otherwise `product_contract_source:<value>` when present; otherwise `none`. Personas that adapt on provenance (product-lens, adversarial, scope-guardian) read this slot to gate technique suppression — they do NOT re-parse frontmatter themselves. |
| `{settled_ktds}` | Session-settled decisions extracted once during Phase 1: any Key Technical Decision **or Product Contract Key Decision** entries carrying a `session-settled:` annotation, listed as decision name, class (`user-directed` / `user-approved`), and rejected alternative; or the literal `none`. Personas read this slot — they do NOT re-parse the document for it. |
| `{document_content}` | Reviewer-specific slice. **Legacy** requirements/plan documents: pass the full document, never split. **Unified** artifacts can be large, so a section slice is the default rather than the full artifact — metadata, Goal Capsule, plus Product Contract for product-lens/adversarial/scope reviewers, and additionally Planning Contract and active Implementation Units/Verification/DoD for feasibility/coherence reviewers when `artifact_readiness: implementation-ready`. Escalate to a broader slice only when a reviewer needs cross-section traceability the initial slice cannot assess. |
| `{decision_primer}` | Round 1: the block below. Round 2+: read `references/decision-primer.md` and render per that file. |

# Decision primer — round 2+

Loaded at Phase 2 dispatch only when the current interactive session has already completed at least one review round. Round 1 uses the inline `<prior-decisions>` block in SKILL.md and does not need this file.

The primer tells each persona what the user already decided, so round N+1 neither re-surfaces rejected findings nor assumes an applied fix landed correctly.

## Rendering

Accumulate every prior round's decisions and render them as:

```
<prior-decisions>
Round 1 — applied (N entries):
- {section}: "{title}" ({reviewer}, {confidence})
  Evidence: "{evidence_snippet}"

Round 1 — rejected (M entries):
- {section}: "{title}" — Skipped because {reason}
  Evidence: "{evidence_snippet}"
- {section}: "{title}" — Deferred to Open Questions because {reason or "no reason provided"}
  Evidence: "{evidence_snippet}"
- {section}: "{title}" — Acknowledged without applying because {reason or "no suggested_fix — user acknowledged"}
  Evidence: "{evidence_snippet}"
- {section}: "{title}" — Withdrawn because {triggering decision}
  Evidence: "{evidence_snippet}"

Round 2 — applied (N entries):
...
</prior-decisions>
```

**Every entry carries an `Evidence:` line.** Synthesis R29 (rejected-finding suppression) and R30 (fix-landed verification) both use an evidence-substring overlap check as part of their matching predicate; without the snippet the orchestrator cannot compute the `>50%` overlap test and falls back to fingerprint-only matching, which either re-surfaces rejected findings or suppresses too aggressively. Use the finding's **first** evidence quote, truncated to ~120 characters on a word boundary, with internal quotes escaped. Remaining evidence entries live in the run artifact and are not needed for the overlap check.

## Which actions count as rejected

Skip, Defer, and Acknowledge are all **rejected-class** — each signals the user decided the finding wasn't worth actioning this round. (Acknowledge is the no-fix-guard variant: the user saw a finding with no `suggested_fix` and recorded acknowledgement instead of an explicit defer or skip; for suppression that is semantically equivalent to Skip.)

**Withdraw is conditional.** It is the revalidation variant — an earlier decision resolved or contradicted the finding (see "Withdrawing findings the user's earlier answers resolved" in `walkthrough.md`):

- Counts as rejected-class **only** when a user decision retired it — a settled premise (Skip/Defer) or a user-asserted fact.
- An **Apply-triggered Withdraw never does.** Its resolution depends on the staged edit both landing and semantically resolving the finding, which round N+1 re-synthesis checks — not R29. Suppressing it would hide a fix that failed or landed ineffectively.

Applied findings stay on the applied list so round-N+1 personas can verify the fixes landed (see R30 in `synthesis-and-presentation.md`).

## Scope

Cross-session persistence is out of scope. A later review of the same document starts at round 1 with no carried primer, even if prior sessions deferred findings into the document's Open Questions section.

**依頼の指定との突き合わせ**
- **skill**: スキル `ce-doc-review` は前回の依頼のときにこのセッションで読み込んでおり、今回もその手順で進めました。レビュアは前回と同じ 4 人 (coherence・feasibility・scope-guardian・adversarial) です。
- **effort**: 指定が空だったので、渡していません。
- **モデル**: 4 人の sub-agent すべてに `opus` を渡しました。
- **手順と違えた点** (トップレベルの `attrs` に理由を書いています):
  - cross-model のレビュー (別の会社のモデルにも読ませる手順) は行っていません。文書を外部へ送ることになり、その承認が無いためです。
  - ce-doc-review が文書へ直接当てる修正は適用していません。作業ツリーの扱いが「共有」なので、それらもすべて findings に入れました。

- **重複の扱い**: 複数のレビュアが同じ問題を挙げたものは 1 件にまとめ、`attrs.reviewers` にそのレビュアを並べました。
- **引用の確認**: 引用した文字列がすべて、指定した行にあることを確かめました。

**P1 の指摘**
1. `PR の報告` (作業のセッションが PR を作ったときに書くコメント) がある Issue を、その PR によらずに閉じたときの扱いが決まっていない。管理のセッションは資源と宣言を解放せず、利用者にも尋ねない。一方で作業のセッションは `stop` を受けて次へ移るので、2 つのセッションの見方が食い違う。
2. レート制限の対処として、コメントとタイムラインを読む範囲を作業中の項目と `Ready` の項目に限っている。この範囲では、KTD19 の表が出どころとして必要とする項目を読めない。
   - 割り当ての無い `Blocked` の項目
   - 待つ相手の Issue
   - 割り当てが終わった後に reopen された項目
3. 経路の表の行「待機の通知・合図」と「利用者の答え」は排他を確かめない。そのため、`--end` で終えたセッションでも、古い待機が終わると記録を読んで書き込める。
4. 宣言を「`Agent session ID` の更新時刻より後」に絞っている。利用者が ID を空にしたときや、項目を Project から除いたときは更新時刻が残らない。その結果、答えを待つ間に資源が空いたと数えられ、別の項目に割り当てられうる。
5. 尋ね直しの間に管理のセッションが書いた `Blocked` が、最新の `待機` の理由が「利用者の答え」であるため、利用者が付けた `Blocked` と読まれる。そのため、利用者が進めると答えても Status が戻らない。

**作業ツリーの確認**
- レビューの前後とも、HEAD は `9395676`、ブランチは `feat/issue-dispatch-plan-114` のままでした。
- `git status --porcelain` の出力は空です。

content.text:
依頼文のとおりにレビューし、結果を [tmp/review-20261018-1044-feat-issue-dispatch-plan-114-11-ce-doc-review-opus.yaml](tmp/review-20261018-1044-feat-issue-dispatch-plan-114-11-ce-doc-review-opus.yaml) に書き出しました。指摘は 23 件 (P1 が 3 件、P2 が 14 件、P3 が 6 件) で、別に 12 行の residual (指摘に数えないが残した観察) があります。

**依頼の指定との突き合わせ**
- **skill**: スキル `ce-doc-review` の手順で、レビュアを sub-agent に依頼しました。レビュアは前回と同じ coherence・feasibility・scope-guardian・adversarial の 4 人です。
- **effort**: 指定が空だったので、渡していません。
- **モデル**: 4 人の sub-agent すべてに `opus` を渡しました。
- **手順と違えた点**: 前回と同じく、次の 3 つです。理由はトップレベルの `attrs` に書いています。
  - cross-model の pass (文書を外部のモデルにも読ませる手順) は行っていません。
  - skill が文書へ直接当てる修正は適用していません。
  - 今回のレビューは、前回までの判定を持ち越さない 1 回目として扱いました。
- **重複の扱い**: 複数のレビュアが同じ問題を挙げたものは 1 件にまとめ、`attrs.reviewers` にそのレビュアを並べました。
- **引用の確認**: 引用は、指定した行にその文字列があることを確かめました。行番号がずれていた 3 か所は、正しい行に直しています。

**P1 の指摘**
1. 増分で「進行中の Issue」を「今の割り当ての PR がマージ済みでない Issue」に変えました。それなのに、待機に渡したレビュー待ちの Issue (`--in-review`) が閉じられると、作業のセッションの待機は PR がマージ済みでなくても `stop` を返すままです。そのため、管理のセッションは利用者に尋ねて割り当てを保ち、作業のセッションは次の Issue へ移り、2 つの見方が食い違います。レビュアは 3 人が挙げました。
2. スキル `issue-work` をやり直したとき、閉じて利用者の答えを待つ Issue は、増分で足した分岐により待機 `wait-decision` に渡されます。しかしこの待機では、`解放` (割り当てを外したことを記録するコメント) も reopen も待てません。宣言に `開始可` が既にある Issue を渡すと、最初の読み取りで `go` を返し、閉じた Issue の作業を再開してしまいます。レビュアは 4 人とも挙げました。

**依頼の指定との突き合わせ**
- **skill**: スキル `ce-doc-review` の手順で、レビュアを sub-agent に依頼しました。レビュアは前回と同じ coherence・feasibility・scope-guardian・adversarial の 4 人です。

  - cross-model の pass (外部のモデルにも文書を読ませる手順) は行っていません。

- **引用の確認**: 引用は、指定した行にその文字列があることを確かめました。
  - 行番号がずれていた 3 か所 (L170・L1194・L1196) は、正しい行に直しました。
  - 文書に無い文言を引いていた 1 か所は、引用から外しました。

**P1 の指摘**
1. 状態「閉じて答えを待つ」の待機 `wait-assignment --closed` は、reopen と `解放` でしか終わりません。この状態のまま PR がマージされると正常な終わりになりますが、待機はそれに気づきません。合図 `stop` が失われると、作業のセッションは `available` を送らないまま待ち続けます。4 人とも挙げた指摘です。

依頼文のとおりにレビューし、結果を [tmp/review-20261018-1612-feat-issue-dispatch-plan-114-13-ce-doc-review-opus.yaml](tmp/review-20261018-1612-feat-issue-dispatch-plan-114-13-ce-doc-review-opus.yaml) に書き出しました。指摘は 20 件で、内訳は P1 が 5 件、P2 が 10 件、P3 が 5 件です。ほかに、指摘には数えない観察を residual に 11 行残しています。

**依頼の指定との突き合わせ**
- **skill**: スキル `ce-doc-review` の手順で、レビュアを sub-agent に依頼しました。レビュアは前回と同じ coherence・feasibility・scope-guardian・adversarial の 4 人です。
- **effort**: 指定が空だったので、渡していません。
- **モデル**: 4 人の sub-agent すべてに `opus` を渡しました。
- **手順と違えた点**: 前回と同じ 3 つで、理由はトップレベルの `attrs` に書いています。
  - cross-model の pass (文書を外部のモデルにも読ませる手順) は行っていません。
  - skill が文書へ直接当てる修正は適用していません。
  - 前回までの判定を持ち越さず、1 回目として扱いました。
- **今回足した扱い**: 増分で Open Questions に「実装の単位で決めること」が加わりました。そこに挙げた項目は、計画のほかの箇所と矛盾する場合を除いて報告しないよう、feasibility と adversarial に依頼しました。このことも `attrs` に書いています。
- **重複の扱い**: 複数のレビュアが同じ問題を挙げたものは 1 件にまとめ、`attrs.reviewers` にそのレビュアを並べました。
- **引用の確認**: 引用は、指定した行にその文字列があることを確かめました。
  - 行番号のずれは無く、引用を 1 か所だけ短くしました (L1439)。
  - 単位の取り違えも 1 か所直しました。指摘 6 の L1630 は U23 のテストです。

**P1 の指摘**
1. 利用者が「解除しない」と答えたら、管理のセッションがフィールドを書き戻すことになりました。しかし、書き戻すサブコマンドもテストもありません。`assign` は空でない値を終了コード 7 で拒否し、AE24 の Then は「書き戻さない」のままです。
2. 利用者が Status を `Todo` にした項目で割り当てを保つと答えても、Status を戻す書き手がいません。作業のセッションの待機 `wait-assignment --pending` は、Status が `In Progress` か `Blocked` にならないと終わらないので、作業が進みません。4 人とも挙げた指摘です。
3. 正常な終わりを「閉じていて、今の割り当ての PR が ready for review かマージ済み」としましたが、どの時点の PR の状態で判定するかが決まっていません。閉じた後に PR が draft に戻されると、解放済みの Issue が進行中に見えて、利用者に尋ね直します。
4. 正常な終わりではコメント `解放` を書きません。そのため合図 `stop` が失われた後に Issue が reopen されると、作業のセッションの待機は終わる手がかりを失い、期限のたびに起動し直し続けます。
5. 「今の割り当ての PR」と `In review` の条件が、KTD19・KTD8・R21・AE6 の間で食い違っています。たとえば `Closes` の無い PR では、正常な終わりか、`In review` にするかの答えが箇所によって変わります。

**作業ツリーの確認**
- レビューの前後とも、HEAD は `1a48d97`、ブランチは `feat/issue-dispatch-plan-114` のままでした。
- `git status --porcelain` の出力は空です。

  - 対象箇所の逐語引用 (行番号つき)。矛盾の主張なら、矛盾する 2 箇所の両方を引く

- テスト・検査の不在を主張する指摘 (「この入力のテストが無い」「この分岐が実行されていない」)
  は、その入力を実際に通して報告が出ないことを確かめてから出す。確かめられなければ
  confidence を low にする。テスト関数名の列挙や grep だけで結論しない — 別名のテストが
  同じ分岐を踏んでいることがある。

報告しない条件 (トリアージで却下される種類):

- 壊れる入力・状態を具体に挙げられない一般的懸念
- 既存の関門 (テスト関数名・検査項目名で挙げられるもの) が、被害が出る前に検出する欠陥 (被害が起きたことが目に見えるだけのものは含まない)

- 整理・統一の好み (放置して壊れるものが無いもの)。リファクタ提案は 1 件まで、その旨を明記して

content.text:
Review target: `52c9a4c..bc0696d`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""issue-dispatch の CLI の入口。サブコマンドごとにパッケージ issue_dispatch のモジュールの関数を実行する。入出力は JSON。
+
+サブコマンドの一覧の正本は、計画 docs/plans/2026-10-06-2025-feat-issue-dispatch-plan.md の KTD14。
+この版にあるサブコマンド:
+  config read --dir <ルート> --role manager|repo   設定を読み、デフォルト値を当てた後の設定と警告・エラーを返す
+  config add-edit-check --dir <ルート> --repo <owner/repo>   管理ディレクトリの設定の third_party_edit_check に足す
+
+終了コード: 0 = 正常。1 = エラーがある (JSON は出す)。2 = 引数の誤り (argparse)。
+停止の条件の正本は同じ計画の R25 (1 と 2 は Python 自身も使うので、サブコマンドの専用の終了コードには使わない)。
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import sys
+
+from issue_dispatch import config
+
+
+def _emit(payload):
+    json.dump(payload, sys.stdout, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
+    sys.stdout.write("\n")
+
+
+def cmd_config_read(args):
+    result = config.load(args.dir, args.role)
+    _emit(result)
+    return 1 if result["errors"] else 0
+
+
+def cmd_config_add_edit_check(args):
+    result = config.add_edit_check(args.dir, args.repo)
+    _emit(result)
+    return 1 if result["errors"] else 0
+
+
+def build_parser():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="issue_dispatch.py", description="issue-dispatch の同梱 CLI (入出力は JSON)")
+    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
+
+    p_config = sub.add_parser("config", help="設定の読み込みと書き換え")
+    config_sub = p_config.add_subparsers(dest="subcommand", required=True)
+
+    p_read = config_sub.add_parser("read", help="設定を読む")
+    p_read.add_argument("--dir", required=True, help="管理ディレクトリかリポジトリのルート")
+    p_read.add_argument("--role", required=True, choices=config.ROLES, help="manager (管理ディレクトリ) / repo (リポジトリ)")
+    p_read.set_defaults(func=cmd_config_read)
+
+    p_add = config_sub.add_parser("add-edit-check", help="third_party_edit_check にリポジトリを足す (承認を得た後)")
+    p_add.add_argument("--dir", required=True, help="管理ディレクトリ")
+    p_add.add_argument("--repo", required=True, help="owner/repo")
+    p_add.set_defaults(func=cmd_config_add_edit_check)
+    return parser
+
+
+def main(argv=None):
+    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
+    return args.func(args)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

2	
3	issue-dispatch は、管理ディレクトリ (管理のセッションが動くディレクトリ) とリポジトリの、同じ相対パス `.claude/akm-claude-plugins/issue-dispatch/config.json` を読む。ファイル名は同じで、キーで役割が分かれる。**この文書が、設定のキーと「未設定」のときの扱いの正本。** 読み込みはモジュール `scripts/issue_dispatch/config.py` が行い、CLI の `config read` で読める (入出力は JSON)。
4	
5	[review-triage](https://github.com/akm/claude-plugins/tree/main/review-triage) と同じ流儀で、プラグインは共通の規則を持ち、リポジトリ固有の宣言だけをこのファイルに書く。
6	
7	## 様式
8	
9	管理ディレクトリの設定:
10	
11	```json
12	{
13	  "project": { "owner": "akm", "number": 3 },
14	  "record_dir": "tmp/issue-dispatch",
15	  "poll_minutes": 3,
16	  "wait_minutes": 60,
17	  "declare_deadline_minutes": 60,
18	  "third_party_edit_check": ["akm/example-public"],
19	  "resources": {
20	    "dev-port": { "capacity": 1, "reserve": "on_declare" }
21	  },
22	  "repositories": {
23	    "akm/example": "/Users/me/src/example"
24	  }
25	}
26	```
27	
28	リポジトリの設定:
29	
30	```json
31	{
32	  "project": { "owner": "akm", "number": 3 },
33	  "files": [
34	    { "pattern": "dist/**", "kind": "generated" },
35	    { "pattern": "docs/**/*.md", "kind": "sectioned", "unit_notation": "heading", "split_reference": "file", "mergeable": true }
36	  ],
37	  "protected_paths": ["infra/prod/"],
38	  "hooks": { "guard_other_worktrees": true },
39	  "poll_minutes": 3,
40	  "wait_minutes": 60
41	}
42	```
43	
44	## キーの表
45	
46	| キー | 置き場 | 意味 | 未設定のときの扱い |
47	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
48	| `project` | 管理 / リポジトリ | Project の `owner` (文字列) と `number` (1 以上の整数)。管理ディレクトリでは、管理のセッションが読む Project。リポジトリでは、`issue-work` が管理のセッションの規約の名前を導くのに使う (1 つだけ書く。ほかの Project の作業をさせるときは `issue-work` の引数 `--manager` で名前を渡す) | 管理ディレクトリでは**必須**で、無ければ `config read` がエラーを返し、管理のセッションは Project の owner と番号を利用者に尋ねて設定の雛形を示す。リポジトリでは省略できる (`issue-work` は開始時に利用者に尋ねる) |
49	| `record_dir` | 管理 | 記録の置き場 (管理ディレクトリからの相対パス)。記録の契約は [records.md](records.md) | `tmp/issue-dispatch` |
50	| `poll_minutes` | 管理 / リポジトリ | 管理ディレクトリでは、管理のセッションのポーリングの間隔 (分)。リポジトリでは、作業のセッションの待機 (`wait-assignment`・`wait-decision`) の間隔 (`--interval`) | 3 |
51	| `wait_minutes` | 管理 / リポジトリ | 管理ディレクトリでは、管理のセッションの待機の期限 (分)。リポジトリでは、作業のセッションの待機の期限 (`--minutes`) | 60 |
52	| `declare_deadline_minutes` | 管理 | 割り当てから着手の宣言までの期限 (分)。過ぎると `Agent stuck state` に `deadline-passed` を書く | 60 |
53	| `third_party_edit_check` | 管理 | 第三者による Issue の本文の編集を割り当ての前に確かめるリポジトリ (`owner/repo`) の配列。管理のセッションが承認を得て `config add-edit-check` で足す | 空 (どのリポジトリも確かめない) |
54	| `resources` | 管理 | 資源の名前ごとの属性 (`capacity`・`reserve`・`when_busy`・`release_undeclared` など)。属性の意味とデフォルト値の正本は [resources.md](resources.md)。1 つの資源を複数のリポジトリの Issue が使うので、Project 全体の設定である管理ディレクトリに書く | 空 (どの資源も、すべての属性がデフォルト値) |
55	| `repositories` | 管理 | リポジトリ (`owner/repo`) ごとの、worktree を作った元の clone のディレクトリの絶対パス。管理のセッションがリポジトリの設定を読むのに使う (読み方の正本は [repositories.md](repositories.md))。マシンごとに違う値なので管理ディレクトリに書く | 空 (どのリポジトリの設定も読めないので、管理のセッションは宣言の判定を止めてパスの設定を頼む) |
56	| `files` | リポジトリ | パスのパターンごとの、ファイルの種類の規則の配列 (下の「`files` の規則の書き方」)。デフォルトの表より先に照合する | 空 (デフォルトの表だけと照合する。どちらのパターンにも一致しないパスは `unknown-content`) |
57	| `protected_paths` | リポジトリ | フックが書き込みを拒否するパス (リポジトリのルートからの相対パス) の配列 | 空 |
58	| `hooks.guard_other_worktrees` | リポジトリ | ほかの worktree と `protected_paths` への操作を拒否するフックを有効にするか (真偽値) | 設定ファイルがあれば真。設定ファイルが無いリポジトリではフックは何もしない |
59	
60	**役割に無いキー (管理ディレクトリの設定に `files` を書くなど) と、表に無いキーは、使わずに警告する。**
61	
62	## 「未設定」の定義 (正本)
63	
64	**キーが「未設定」とは、キーが無いことだけを指す。** 整数のキー (`poll_minutes`・`wait_minutes`・`declare_deadline_minutes`) の空文字列は未設定と読まず、値の誤りとして扱う。
65	
66	**値の誤り (型が違う・整数が 1 未満・配列の要素の形が違う) は、そのキーをデフォルト値にして続行し、警告を返す。** 止めない。`poll_minutes` が `wait_minutes` 以上のときは、2 つとも値の誤りとして警告し、両方をデフォルト値に戻す (間隔が期限以上だと、待機が 1 回読むごとに期限で終わって送り直しが増えるため)。警告は、管理のセッションの開始時の検査と `repo-preflight` の報告に出す。
67	
68	**読めない設定 (JSON として読めない・最上位がオブジェクトでない) は、エラーとして返し、デフォルト値で続ける。** `config add-edit-check` は読めない設定を上書きしない。
69	
70	`project` の形の誤り (owner が無い・number が整数でない) は、管理ディレクトリではエラー (デフォルト値が無いため)。
71	
72	## `files` の規則の書き方
73	
74	要素は `pattern` と `kind` が必須で、`unit_notation`・`split_reference`・`mergeable` は省略できる。**`kind` と省略できる属性の意味、パターンの照合の規則、デフォルトの表の正本は [file-kinds.md](file-kinds.md)** — この文書は様式と、読み込むときにそろえる表記だけを定める。
75	
76	| キー | 必須 | 内容 |
77	| --- | --- | --- |
78	| `pattern` | ✓ | パスのパターン (リポジトリのルートからの相対パス) |
79	| `kind` | ✓ | ファイルの種類 (値の一覧は file-kinds.md) |
80	| `unit_notation` | | 節の表記とキーの深さ。宣言の `units` と混同しないよう名前を分けている |
81	| `split_reference` | | 分けたときの参照のされ方 (`directory` / `file`) |
82	| `mergeable` | | マージできるか (真偽値) |
83	
84	**読み込むときに `pattern` の表記をそろえる**: 先頭の `./` を取り除き、`//` を `/` にする。末尾の `/` は取り除かない (`posixpath.normpath` を使わないのは、`dist/` を `dist` という名前のファイルだけに一致するパターンに変えてしまうため)。**絶対パス (`/` で始まる) と `..` を含むパターンは、その規則を使わずに警告する** (ルートの外を指しうるため)。`pattern` か `kind` の無い要素も、使わずに警告する。
85	
86	| 書いた値 | そろえた後 |
87	| --- | --- |
88	| `./dist/**` | `dist/**` |
89	| `dist//**` | `dist/**` |
90	| `docs/` | `docs/` (そのまま) |
91	| `/dist/**` | 使わない (警告) |
92	| `../x/**` | 使わない (警告) |
93	
94	## CLI
95	
96	```sh
97	python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/issue_dispatch.py" config read --dir <ルート> --role manager
98	python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/issue_dispatch.py" config read --dir <ルート> --role repo
99	python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/issue_dispatch.py" config add-edit-check --dir <管理ディレクトリ> --repo <owner/repo>
100	```
101	
102	`config read` の出力は `{"status", "path", "role", "config", "warnings", "errors"}` で、`status` は `ok` / `missing` (設定ファイルが無い) / `unreadable` (読めない)。`config` はデフォルト値を当てた後の値。`warnings` と `errors` の要素は `{"key", "message"}`。終了コードは、`errors` があれば 1、無ければ 0。引数の誤りは 2。

findings.failure_scenario: リポジトリの設定ファイルの JSON を書き損じると、status=unreadable で guard_other_worktrees=false になり、ほかの worktree への操作を拒否するフックが、利用者に気づかれないまま無効になる。

findings.summary: config read は設定の errors (初回の project の欠けを含む) で終了コード 1 を返すが、Python の例外で落ちたときも 1 なので、呼び出し側が区別できない。docstring も「1 と 2 は Python 自身も使うので専用の終了コードに使わない」と書き、自分の規則と食い違う。
findings.short_summary: 設定のエラーと異常終了が同じ終了コード 1
findings.failure_scenario: 設定の無い管理ディレクトリで config read を実行すると終了コード 1 になり、traceback で落ちたときと同じ値なので、スキルは終了コードだけでは「雛形を示す」か「スクリプトの不具合として止まる」かを選べない。

findings.summary: add_edit_check は、既存の third_party_edit_check が配列でないと、警告もせずに捨てて [repo] で上書きする。
findings.short_summary: 配列でない既存の値を警告なしに上書きする
findings.failure_scenario: 利用者が "third_party_edit_check": "akm/x" と書いていると、add-edit-check --repo akm/y の後のファイルは ["akm/y"] になり、akm/x が消えたことが返り値にも出ない。

findings.summary: add_edit_check は --dir が存在しなくてもディレクトリを作って設定を書くので、打ち間違えたパスに新しい設定ができる。
findings.short_summary: 存在しない --dir にも設定を作る

findings.failure_scenario: files の pattern に docs/./a.md と書くと、そのまま採用され、docs/a.md のパスに一致しない規則になるが、警告は出ない。

- このことも、YAML のトップレベルの `attrs.worktree_incident` に書いています。

- `git status --porcelain` の出力は空です。
- 残したのは出力先の 1 ファイルだけで、コミットはしていません。

Review target: `bc0696d..cbf8bc9`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

9	種類は、パスについて次の問いに上から順に答え、最初に当てはまったものにする。1 つのパスが種類の違う複数の規則に一致すれば、この表で先の種類にする (下の「照合の順」)。
10	
11	| 段 | 問い | 当てはまれば | 競合の可能性の判定 | 競合の可能性があるときに示す扱い |
12	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
13	| 1 | 内容を知らない (パスに一致するパターンが、リポジトリの設定にもデフォルトの表にも無い) | `unknown-content` | 同じパスなら、競合しうるかどうかを利用者に尋ねる | — |
14	| 2 | ツールが生成する | `generated` | 判定しない | — |
15	| 3 | 構造を知らない | `unknown-structure` | 同じパスなら競合しうる | 待つ・共通の変更を先に小さな PR にする・競合しうるまま進める、の 3 つ |
16	| 4 | 分割できない | `indivisible` | 節で判定する (下) | 同上 |
17	| 5 | 分割すると意味が変わる可能性がある | `unstable` | 節で判定する | 同上。共通の変更を先にする小さな PR で、分けるリファクタリングも行える (意味が変わりうる点を添える) |
18	| 6 | (上のどれでもない) | `divisible` | 節で判定する | 同上。共通の変更を先にする小さな PR で、分けるリファクタリングも行える |
19	
20	`unknown-content` は、どの規則にも一致しないパスの種類なので、規則の `kind` には書けない。規則に書ける種類は段 2〜6 の 5 つ。
21	
22	節 (unit) は種類ではなく、構造を知っている種類 (段 4〜6) の判定の細かさとして扱う。
23	
24	**レビューでの修正による競合の可能性は判定しない。** 競合しうる相手とのマージの衝突は利用者が解消する (レビューで変わる範囲は宣言の時点で決まらないため)。
25	
26	## 節で判定する
27	
28	構造を知っている種類 (`indivisible`・`unstable`・`divisible`) は、両方の宣言がそのパスに `units` を書いていれば、節が同じか、一方の配列が他方の配列の先頭部分 (`["dependencies"]` と `["dependencies", "react"]` など) のときだけ競合しうる。`["dependencies", "react"]` と `["dependencies", "zod"]` は競合しない。どちらかが `units` を省けば、同じパスで競合しうる。
29	
30	節は階層ごとの名前の配列で表す (`["dependencies", "zod"]`)。区切りの文字を使わないのは、名前に `.` や `/` が含まれることがあるため (`package.json` の `exports` のキー `./utils`、`go.mod` のモジュール名 `github.com/foo/bar`、見出し「v1.2 の変更」)。名前はファイルにある文字のまま比べ、正規化しない (`"./utils"` と `"utils"` は JSON では別のキー)。節の名前は作業のセッションがファイルを読んで書き、スクリプトは名前を比べるだけで、ファイルを構文解析しない。
31	
32	## 節の表記 (`unit_notation`)
33	
34	規則の `unit_notation` は、そのファイルの節をどの構造の名前で書くかを示す。宣言の `units` と混同しないよう名前を分けている。
35	
36	| 構造 | 表記 | 例 (節の配列) |
37	| --- | --- | --- |
38	| JSON のキー | `json-key` | `["dependencies", "zod"]`・`["exports", "./utils"]` |
39	| YAML のキー | `yaml-key` | `["jobs", "test"]` |
40	| TOML のテーブル | `toml-table` | `["tool", "ruff"]` |
41	| Markdown の見出しと frontmatter | `markdown-heading` | `["手順", "1. 入力を読む"]`・`["frontmatter", "title"]` |
42	| Makefile のターゲット | `make-target` | `["test"]` |
43	| `go.mod` のディレクティブ | `go-mod-directive` | `["require", "github.com/foo/bar"]` |
44	| Dockerfile のステージ | `dockerfile-stage` | `["builder"]` |
45	| Terraform のブロック | `terraform-block` | `["resource", "aws_s3_bucket", "logs"]` |
46	
47	値は、表記の名前の文字列 (`"markdown-heading"`) か、表記とキーの深さを持つオブジェクト `{"notation": "json-key", "keys": ["dependencies", "devDependencies"]}` のどちらか。`keys` は、そのキーの下を 1 つ下の階層ごとの節として扱うキーの配列で、`package.json` では `dependencies` の下を依存ごとの節にする。`keys` に無いキーは、そのキー全体が 1 つの節になる。`keys` は `json-key`・`yaml-key`・`toml-table` でだけ意味を持つ。
48	
49	`unit_notation` の無い規則のファイル (`.go`・`.ts` など) は、節の表記を決めていないので、宣言に `units` を書かない。
50	
51	## パターンの書き方
52	
53	- `*` は 1 つのディレクトリの名前の中だけで一致し (`/` を越えない)、`**` は 0 個以上のディレクトリに一致する。`?` は `/` 以外の 1 文字。
54	- パターンは、リポジトリのルートからのパス全体と照合する。`*.pb.go` はルートのファイルだけに一致し、どの階層にも一致させるには `**/*.pb.go` と書く。
55	- 末尾が `/` のパターン (`dist/`) は、そのディレクトリの下のすべて (`dist/**`) と同じに扱う。
56	
57	Python 3.13 の `PurePath.full_match` と同じ規則で、`.gitignore` や `.gitattributes` の規則 (`/` を含まないパターンがどの階層にも一致する) とは違う。Python 3.11 には `full_match` が無く、`fnmatch` は `*` が `/` を越えて一致するので、`filekinds` はパターンを正規表現に変換して照合する。
58	
59	| パターン | 一致する | 一致しない |
60	| --- | --- | --- |
61	| `*.pb.go` | `api.pb.go` | `gen/api.pb.go` |
62	| `**/*.pb.go` | `api.pb.go`・`gen/api.pb.go` | |
63	| `src/*.ts` | `src/app.ts` | `src/lib/a.ts` |
64	| `dist/` | `dist/app.js`・`dist/assets/a.js` | `dist` (ディレクトリそのものの名前)・`distribution/a.js` |
65	
66	## 照合の順
67	
68	1. リポジトリの設定の `files` の規則を先に、デフォルトの表を後に照合する。設定に一致する規則があれば、デフォルトの表は見ない。
69	2. 同じ側 (設定、またはデフォルトの表) で種類の違う複数の規則に一致すれば、6 段の表で先の種類の規則を選ぶ。規則の並び順では決めない。
70	3. どちらにも一致しなければ `unknown-content`。
71	
72	設定の規則がデフォルトの表より先なのは、同じ拡張子でも扱いがリポジトリで違うため (同じ `.js` でも、自前で書いたものと、`.ts` やビルドから生成したものがある)。種類は拡張子ではなくパスのパターンで決める。
73	
74	## 分けたときの参照のされ方 (`split_reference`)
75	
76	`unstable` と `divisible` の規則には、ほかのファイルがそのファイルをどう参照するか (`split_reference`) を書く。共通の変更を先にする小さな PR で、ファイルを分けるリファクタリングを行うときに、参照元を宣言に含めるかを決めるため。
77	
78	| 値 | 意味 | 例 |
79	| --- | --- | --- |
80	| `directory` | 参照元のファイルがディレクトリを指定する。同じディレクトリの中で分けるかぎり参照元は変わらない | Go の `import` のパッケージ、Terraform のモジュール |
81	| `file` | 参照元のファイルがファイルを指定する。分けると参照元も変わるので、リファクタリングの宣言には変わる参照元も含める | TypeScript の `import './app'`・Makefile の `include`・CSS の `@import` |
82	
83	## マージできないファイル (`mergeable`)
84	
85	画像など、差分でマージできないファイルは、規則に `"mergeable": false` を書く (省略は真)。そのファイルで「競合しうるまま進める」を選ぼうとしたら、後で衝突を直せないことを添えて尋ねる。
86	
87	## 共有の状態を持つファイル
88	
89	`terraform.tfstate` のように、ファイルが共有の状態 (実際のインフラ) を記録しているものは、種類 (`generated`) とは別に資源 (ラベル `resource:…`) として扱う。種類はファイルの変更の競合の可能性を判定するもので、共有の状態の取り合いは資源で判定する。
90	
91	## デフォルトの表
92	
93	表そのものの正本は `file-kinds.json` で、ここでは行を言い直さない。行は、パターンと種類と、この文書の各節の属性 (`unit_notation`・`split_reference`・`mergeable`) を持ち、`filekinds` は設定の規則と同じ規則で照合する。各行を選んだ理由は次のとおり。
94	
95	- **`generated`** — ツールが書き、人が編集しないもの: Protocol Buffers の出力 (`**/*.pb.go`)、生成の印を名前に持つ Go のファイル (`**/*_generated.go`)、パッケージマネージャのロックファイル (`**/package-lock.json`・`**/yarn.lock`・`**/pnpm-lock.yaml`・`**/go.sum`・`**/Cargo.lock`)、縮小した JavaScript と CSS (`**/*.min.js`・`**/*.min.css`)、Terraform の状態 (`**/terraform.tfstate*`。共有の状態は上のとおり資源でも扱う)。
96	- **`unknown-structure`** — 中身を読んで節を決められないもの: Excel のブック (`**/*.xlsx`)。
97	- **`indivisible` で `mergeable` が偽** — 画像とフォントとバイナリの文書 (`**/*.png`・`**/*.jpg`・`**/*.jpeg`・`**/*.gif`・`**/*.svg`・`**/*.ico`・`**/*.pdf`・`**/*.woff`・`**/*.woff2`)。分けられず、差分でマージできない。SVG はテキストだが、描画ツールが全体を書き直すので画像と同じに扱う。
98	- **`unstable`** — 分けると適用の順や意味が変わりうるもの: マイグレーション (`**/migrations/**`) と SQL (`**/*.sql`) は実行の順に意味があり、Protocol Buffers の定義 (`**/*.proto`) はフィールド番号の割り当てに意味がある。参照のされ方は `file`。
99	- **`divisible` で節の表記があるもの** — `**/package.json` (`json-key`。`dependencies` と `devDependencies` の下を依存ごとの節にする)、`**/go.mod` (`go-mod-directive`。参照のされ方は `directory`)、`**/*.md` (`markdown-heading`)、`**/Makefile` (`make-target`)、`**/*.toml` (`toml-table`)、`**/*.yaml`・`**/*.yml` (`yaml-key`)、`**/Dockerfile` (`dockerfile-stage`)、`**/*.tf` (`terraform-block`。参照のされ方は `directory`)。
100	- **`divisible` で節の表記の無いもの** — 自前で書くソースコード: `**/*.go` (参照のされ方は `directory`)、`**/*.ts`・`**/*.tsx`・`**/*.js`・`**/*.py`・`**/*.rb`・`**/*.css` (参照のされ方は `file`)。節の表記を決めていないので、宣言に `units` は書けない。
101	
102	リポジトリで扱いが違うもの (生成した `.js`・`.gitattributes` で `linguist-generated` にしたディレクトリなど) は、リポジトリの設定の `files` に書く。候補はスキル `repo-preflight` が示す。

Review target: `53899a3..01b415b`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## If findings are fixed later
