   207	def simplify_item(node, position):
   208	    """GraphQL の項目を、後の単位が読む形にする。Issue 以外の項目 (draft issue・PR) は content を None にして返す。"""
   209	    content = node.get("content") or {}
   210	    fields = {}
   211	    status = None
   212	    for fv in node["fieldValues"]["nodes"]:
   213	        if not fv or not fv.get("field"):
   214	            continue
   215	        name = fv["field"]["name"]
   216	        if name == "Status":
   217	            status = {"name": fv.get("name"), "option_id": fv.get("optionId"), "updated_at": fv.get("updatedAt")}
   218	        elif "text" in fv:
   219	            fields[name] = {"text": fv.get("text"), "updated_at": fv.get("updatedAt")}
   220	        else:
   221	            fields[name] = {"name": fv.get("name"), "option_id": fv.get("optionId"), "updated_at": fv.get("updatedAt")}
   222	    item = {"item_id": node["id"], "position": position, "item_updated_at": node.get("updatedAt"), "status": status, "fields": fields,
   223	            "content_type": content.get("__typename"), "key": None}
   224	    if content.get("__typename") != "Issue":
   225	        return item, []
   226	    repo = content["repository"]["nameWithOwner"]
   227	    sub = content.get("subIssuesSummary") or {}
   228	    parent = content.get("parent")
   229	    item.update({
   230	        "key": _ref(content), "repo": repo, "number": content["number"], "url": content["url"], "title": content["title"],
   231	        "state": content["state"], "created_at": content.get("createdAt"), "author": (content.get("author") or {}).get("login"),
   232	        "visibility": content["repository"].get("visibility"), "in_organization": content["repository"].get("isInOrganization"),
   233	        "assignees": [a["login"] for a in content["assignees"]["nodes"]],
   234	        "labels": [l["name"] for l in content["labels"]["nodes"]],
   235	        "parent": _ref(parent) if parent and parent.get("repository") else None,
   236	        "sub_issues": {"total": sub.get("total", 0), "completed": sub.get("completed", 0)},
   237	        "is_parent": bool(sub.get("total")),
   238	        "blocked_by": [{"key": _ref(b), "url": b["url"], "state": b["state"]} for b in content["blockedBy"]["nodes"]],
   239	        "body_edits": [{"editor": (e.get("editor") or {}).get("login"), "edited_at": e.get("editedAt"), "deleted_at": e.get("deletedAt")}
   240	                       for e in content["userContentEdits"]["nodes"]],
   241	        "prs": [{"number": p["number"], "url": p["url"], "state": p["state"], "draft": p["isDraft"], "merged": p["merged"],
   242	                 "created_at": p.get("createdAt"), "merged_at": p.get("mergedAt"), "closed_at": p.get("closedAt"),
   243	                 "author": (p.get("author") or {}).get("login"), "base_ref": p.get("baseRefName")}
   244	                for p in content["closedByPullRequestsReferences"]["nodes"]],
   245	    })
   246	    problems = []
   247	    comments, problem = _more_pages("issue-comments", repo, content["number"], content["comments"], "comments", _comment)
   248	    if problem:
   249	        problems.append({"item": item["key"], "what": "comments", **problem})
   250	    events, problem = _more_pages("issue-timeline", repo, content["number"], content["timelineItems"], "timelineItems", _event)
   251	    if problem:
   252	        problems.append({"item": item["key"], "what": "events", **problem})
   253	    item["comments"] = comments
   254	    item["events"] = sorted(events, key=lambda e: (e.get("at") or "", EVENT_TYPES.index(e["type"]) if e["type"] in EVENT_TYPES else 99))
   255	    return item, problems

   258	def items(project):
   259	    """項目の一覧を位置の順に全部読む。返り値: {"status": "ok", "project_id", "items": [...], "problems": [...], "rate_limit"} か
   260	    {"status": "error", ...} (最初のページが読めないとき)。続きのページやコメントの続きが読めなかったときは problems に入れて止める。"""
   261	    result_items = []
   262	    problems = []
   263	    after = None
   264	    project_id = None
   265	    rate = None
   266	    position = 0
   267	    while True:
   268	        data, problem = graphql("items", {"owner": project["owner"], "number": project["number"], "after": after})
   269	        if problem:
   270	            if not result_items:
   271	                return {"status": "error", **problem}
   272	            problems.append({"what": "items-page", "after": after, **problem})
   273	            break
   274	        node = _project_node(data)
   275	        if node is None:
   276	            return {"status": "error", "failure": "other", "message": f"Project {project['owner']}/{project['number']} が無いか読めない", "exit_code": 0}
   277	        project_id = node["id"]
   278	        rate = data.get("rateLimit")
   279	        for n in node["items"]["nodes"]:
   280	            if not n:
   281	                continue
   282	            position += 1
   283	            item, item_problems = simplify_item(n, position)
   284	            result_items.append(item)
   285	            problems += item_problems
   286	        info = node["items"].get("pageInfo") or {}
   287	        if not info.get("hasNextPage"):
   288	            break
   289	        after = info.get("endCursor")
   290	    return {"status": "ok" if not problems else "partial", "project_id": project_id, "items": result_items, "problems": problems, "rate_limit": rate}

   303	    r = gh.run(["project", "item-edit", "--project-id", meta_project["id"], "--id", item_id, "--field-id", field["id"],

   305	    if r["failure"]:
   306	        return {"status": "error", "failure": r["failure"], "message": r["stderr_tail"]}

## 作り方 (`project check` と `project add-fields`)

`project check` は、フィールド 3 つの有無と型、`Agent stuck state` の値、Status の選択肢、ワークフローを確かめ、不足と作る手順の案を返す (読むだけ)。利用者の承認を得てから `project add-fields` が案を実行する。

- フィールドは `gh project field-create <番号> --owner <owner> --name <名前> --data-type TEXT|SINGLE_SELECT [--single-select-options <値,…>]` で作る。
- Status の選択肢は GraphQL の `updateProjectV2Field` (`singleSelectOptions`) で足す。**既存の選択肢を `id` 付きで含めて渡す** — 含めないと既存の値が消える (U1 で確かめた)。足す選択肢の色と説明: `Ready` は GREEN「着手してよい」、`In review` は BLUE「PR が ready for review」、`Blocked` は RED「ほかの Issue か小さな PR を待つ」。既存の項目の Status の値は変わらない。

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

増分 `c051a54..a583863` をレビューしました。前回の 4 件は解消しています。ただし、この増分で新しく生じた指摘が 1 件あります。

**結果のファイル:** `tmp/review-20261022-0731-feat-issue-dispatch-u7-project-114-2-code-review-opus.yaml`

**レビューの実行**
- Skill ツールで code-review を、引数 `high c051a54..a583863` で呼びました。
- effort は `high` を渡しました。
- モデルはこのセッションの opus です。code-review は sub-agent を使わずにこの文脈で進める手順なので、モデルを別に渡す場所はありませんでした。
- ReportFindings も呼び、同じ 1 件を渡しました。

**指摘 (P3・confidence medium)** — ファイル `issue-dispatch/scripts/issue_dispatch.py` の L211
- コミット 82aaec3 で、関数 `read_meta` は、GraphQL がデータと errors を一緒に返したときも status `ok` と `warnings` を返すようになりました。
- CLI の `project add-fields` は `warnings` を見ないまま、その一部だけのデータで案を実行します。そのため、null で返ったフィールドを無いものとみなして、もう一度作ります。結果として、同じ名前のフィールドが 2 つできます。
- 偽の gh で確かめた結果: フィールド `Agent session ID` を null にした応答では、関数 `check` が `field-create Agent session ID` の案を出しました。
- 増分の前は、この場面で `read_meta` が error を返して止まっていました。

**`residual` に入れたもの**
- 前回の 4 件が解消したこと。主な修正は次の 2 つです。
  - GraphQL の変数を `gh api graphql --input -` の本文で渡すようになった。
  - 入れ子の connection が 1 ページに収まらないときは、`problems` に入れて知らせるようになった。
- 関数 `_more_pages` は、続きのページでデータと一緒に返った errors を捨てます。最初のページでは知らせているので、扱いが揃っていません。
- 関数 `gh.run` は、標準入力を渡さないときに `/dev/null` を使うようになりました。gh が利用者に入力を求める場面では、待たずに失敗します。

**テスト**
- 158 件すべて成功しました。

**作業ツリー**
- 確認のスクリプトを動かす前に、偽の gh の置き場をシンボリックリンクで確かめました。
  - 偽の gh に届いたことは、記録ファイル (`FAKE_GH_ARGS`) で確かめました。今回は本物の gh は実行していません。
- HEAD はレビューの前後とも a583863 です。
- `git status --porcelain` と `git status --porcelain --ignored issue-dispatch` は、どちらも何も出しませんでした。
- `__pycache__` は作られていません。
- 確認のためのファイルは scratchpad にだけ作りました。作業ツリーに作ったのは結果の YAML の 1 つだけで、コミットはしていません。

content.text: (Re-invocation of /code-review — the skill instructions were previously loaded; the arguments or dynamic output below are new.)

Review target: `a583863..8528090`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

Review target: `f9995ce..5e7aa72`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

content.text: (Re-invocation of /code-review — the skill instructions were previously loaded; the arguments or dynamic output below are new.)

Review target: `5e7aa72..b57c619`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

content.text: (Re-invocation of /code-review — the skill instructions were previously loaded; the arguments or dynamic output below are new.)

Review target: `17d3247..49c3f29`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

   155	def _wait_text(w):

   165	def _value_fields(kind, values):

   182	def format_header(role, name, session_id, kind, values=None):
   183	    """先頭行を作る。role は manager / worker。値の形は normalize_values。名前は区切り文字を含んでもよい (解析は右から読む) が、
   184	    セッション ID は含めない。種類が役割のものでない・値が足りないなどは ValueError。"""
   185	    if role not in ROLES:
   186	        raise ValueError(f"役割は manager か worker: {role!r}")
   187	    if kind not in (MANAGER_KINDS if role == "manager" else WORKER_KINDS):
   188	        raise ValueError(f"種類 {kind!r} は {ROLES[role]}のコメントではない")
   189	    if not isinstance(name, str) or not name.strip() or "\n" in name:
   190	        raise ValueError(f"セッションの名前が無いか、改行を含む: {name!r}")
   191	    if not isinstance(session_id, str) or not session_id.strip() or SEP in session_id or "\n" in session_id or session_id.strip() in _SHAPE:

   194	    return SEP.join([PREFIX, ROLES[role], name.strip(), session_id.strip(), kind] + _value_fields(kind, normalized))

   199	def _split_value(field):

   201	    for word in sorted(VALUE_WORDS, key=len, reverse=True):

   207	def _parse_wait(text):
   208	    for kind in ("利用者の答え", "設定"):
   209	        if text == kind:
   210	            return {"kind": kind}
   211	    if text.startswith("Issue "):
   212	        return {"kind": "Issue", "issue": text[len("Issue "):]}
   213	    if text.startswith("小さな PR "):
   214	        rest = text[len("小さな PR "):]
   215	        issue, _, pr = rest.partition(" PR ")
   216	        out = {"kind": "小さな PR", "issue": issue}
   217	        if pr:
   218	            out["pr"] = pr
   219	        return out
   220	    if text.startswith("資源 "):

   225	def parse_wait_reason(text):
   226	    """`理由 ` の後の文字列 (`利用者の答え` / `Issue <参照>` / `小さな PR <参照> [PR <URL>]` / `資源 <名前>` / `設定`) を
   227	    待つ理由の dict にする。CLI の --reason も同じ形。形が違えば ValueError。"""

   231	def parse_header(line):
   232	    """先頭行を読む。返り値は {"role", "name", "session_id", "kind", "values"} か、先頭行の形でなければ None。
   233	
   234	    右から読む: 値の見出し語で始まる区切りを値として取り、次が種類、その前がセッション ID、残りがすべて名前。名前が
   235	    区切り文字を含んでもよいのはこのため (セッション ID は含まない前提)。値の形が種類に合わなければ None。
   236	    """
   237	    if not isinstance(line, str) or "\n" in line:
   238	        return None
   239	    fields = line.rstrip().split(SEP)
   240	    if len(fields) < 5 or fields[0] != PREFIX or fields[1] not in _ROLE_OF:
   241	        return None
   242	    role = _ROLE_OF[fields[1]]
   243	    value_fields = []
   244	    index = len(fields) - 1
   245	    while index >= 4 and fields[index] not in _SHAPE and _split_value(fields[index]) is not None:
   246	        value_fields.insert(0, _split_value(fields[index]))
   247	        index -= 1
   248	    if index < 4 or fields[index] not in _SHAPE:
   249	        return None
   250	    kind = fields[index]
   251	    if kind not in (MANAGER_KINDS if role == "manager" else WORKER_KINDS):
   252	        return None
   253	    session_id = fields[index - 1]
   254	    name = SEP.join(fields[2:index - 1])
   255	    if not name or not session_id:
   256	        return None
   257	    raw = {}
   258	    try:
   259	        for word, text in value_fields:
   260	            if word == "理由" and kind == "待機":
   261	                raw.setdefault("waits", []).append(_parse_wait(text))
   262	            elif word == "理由" and kind == "解放":
   263	                raw["release_reason"] = text
   264	            elif word == "Issue" and kind == "依存の待ち":
   265	                raw.setdefault("blockers", []).append(text)
   266	            else:
   267	                key = next((k for k, w in _WORD_OF.items() if w == word and k not in ("waits", "blockers", "release_reason")), None)
   268	                if key is None or key in raw:
   269	                    return None
   270	                raw[key] = text
   271	        values = normalize_values(kind, raw)
   272	    except ValueError:

   274	    return {"role": role, "name": name, "session_id": session_id, "kind": kind, "values": values}

   277	def split_body(body):
   278	    """コメントの本文を (先頭行の解析結果か None, 先頭行と空行を除いた本文) にする。先頭行の形でなければ本文はそのまま。"""

   280	    first, _, rest = text.partition("\n")

   289	def token_login():
   290	    r = gh.run(["api", "user"], expect_json=True)
   291	    login = (r["json"] or {}).get("login") if isinstance(r["json"], dict) else None
   292	    if r["failure"] or not login:
   293	        return None, {"status": "error", "failure": r["failure"] or "other", "exit_code": r["exit_code"],
   294	                      "message": r["stderr_tail"] or r.get("json_error") or "gh api user でログインを読めない"}
   295	    return login, None

   298	def list_comments(issue, login=None):
   299	    """Issue のコメントを時刻の順に全部読む。書き手がトークンのログイン (login。None なら `gh api user`) と違うコメントは除く
   300	    (R6。公開リポジトリでは第三者も書けるため)。返り値: {"status": "ok", "login", "comments": [{id, database_id, url,
   301	    created_at, author, header (parse_header の結果か None), body (先頭行を除いた本文)}], "excluded" (除いた件数), "rate_limit"}
   302	    か失敗の説明。"""
   303	    ref = ids.parse_issue_ref(issue)
   304	    if ref is None:
   305	        return {"status": "error", "failure": "other", "exit_code": None, "message": f"Issue の参照ではない: {issue!r}"}
   306	    if login is None:
   307	        login, problem = token_login()
   308	        if problem:
   309	            return problem
   310	    owner, _, name = ref["repo"].partition("/")
   311	    nodes, after, rate_limit = [], None, None
   312	    while True:
   313	        data, problem, errors = graphql("issue-comments", {"owner": owner, "name": name, "number": ref["number"], "after": after})
   314	        if problem:
   315	            return {"status": "error", **problem}
   316	        issue_node = (data.get("repository") or {}).get("issue")
   317	        if not issue_node or errors:
   318	            return {"status": "error", "failure": "other", "exit_code": 0,
   319	                    "message": f"Issue {ref['key']} のコメントを読めない: {errors!r}"}
   320	        page = issue_node["comments"]
   321	        nodes += [n for n in page["nodes"] if n]
   322	        rate_limit = data.get("rateLimit") or rate_limit
   323	        info = page.get("pageInfo") or {}
   324	        if not info.get("hasNextPage"):
   325	            break
   326	        after = info.get("endCursor")
   327	    out, excluded = [], 0
   328	    for n in sorted(nodes, key=lambda n: (n.get("createdAt") or "", n.get("databaseId") or 0)):
   329	        if (n.get("author") or {}).get("login") != login:
   330	            excluded += 1
   331	            continue
   332	        header, body = split_body(n.get("body"))
   333	        out.append({"id": n["id"], "database_id": n.get("databaseId"), "url": n.get("url"), "created_at": n.get("createdAt"),
   334	                    "author": login, "header": header, "body": body})
   335	    return {"status": "ok", "login": login, "comments": out, "excluded": excluded, "rate_limit": rate_limit}

   338	# --- 既投稿の見分けと投稿 ---------------------------------------------------------
   339	
   340	def header_key(parsed):
   341	    """同じ出来事かを比べるための鍵。名前は比べない (変わりうる)。書き手の ID・種類・値を比べる。"""
   342	    return (parsed["role"], parsed["session_id"], parsed["kind"], _freeze(parsed["values"]))
   343	
   344	
   345	def _freeze(value):
   346	    if isinstance(value, dict):
   347	        return tuple(sorted((k, _freeze(v)) for k, v in value.items()))
   348	    if isinstance(value, list):
   349	        return tuple(_freeze(v) for v in value)
   350	    return value

   353	def already_posted(parsed, own_comments):
   354	    """同じ出来事への同じコメントが既にあればそのコメント (list_comments の要素) を、無ければ None を返す (KTD2)。
   355	
   356	    own_comments は list_comments が返した、書き手が自分のコメントの配列 (時刻の順)。種類ごとの規則:
   357	    `待機` は同じ宣言への最新の `待機` とだけ比べる。`依存の待ち` は最新の `依存の待ち` と比べ、間に `依存の解消` があれば
   358	    投稿する。`依存の解消` は最新の `依存の待ち` より後のコメントとだけ比べる。`停滞` は同じ対象・割り当て・値なら、間に
   359	    別のコメントがあっても既投稿。ほかの種類は、先頭行の鍵 (header_key) が同じコメントがあれば既投稿。
   360	    """
   361	    kind = parsed["kind"]
   362	    key = header_key(parsed)
   363	    headed = [c for c in own_comments if c.get("header")]
   364	    if kind == "待機":
   365	        same_declaration = [c for c in headed if c["header"]["kind"] == "待機"
   366	                            and c["header"]["values"].get("declaration") == parsed["values"].get("declaration")]
   367	        latest = same_declaration[-1] if same_declaration else None
   368	        return latest if latest and header_key(latest["header"]) == key else None
   369	    if kind == "依存の待ち":
   370	        latest_wait, resolved_after = None, False
   371	        for c in headed:
   372	            if c["header"]["kind"] == "依存の待ち":
   373	                latest_wait, resolved_after = c, False
   374	            elif c["header"]["kind"] == "依存の解消" and latest_wait is not None:
   375	                resolved_after = True
   376	        if latest_wait is None or resolved_after:
   377	            return None
   378	        return latest_wait if header_key(latest_wait["header"]) == key else None
   379	    if kind == "依存の解消":
   380	        after_latest_wait = []
   381	        for c in headed:
   382	            if c["header"]["kind"] == "依存の待ち":
   383	                after_latest_wait = []
   384	            else:
   385	                after_latest_wait.append(c)
   386	        return next((c for c in after_latest_wait if header_key(c["header"]) == key), None)
   387	    if kind == "停滞":
   388	        v = parsed["values"]
   389	        return next((c for c in headed if c["header"]["kind"] == "停滞" and c["header"]["role"] == parsed["role"]
   390	                     and c["header"]["session_id"] == parsed["session_id"]
   391	                     and (c["header"]["values"]["to"], c["header"]["values"]["assignment"], c["header"]["values"]["stuck_state"])
   392	                     == (v["to"], v["assignment"], v["stuck_state"])), None)
   393	    return next((c for c in headed if header_key(c["header"]) == key), None)

   396	def post(issue, role, name, session_id, kind, values, body, login=None):
   397	    """コメントを投稿する。先頭行は format_header で作り、同じ出来事への同じコメントが既にあれば投稿しない (already_posted)。
   398	    返り値: {"status": "ok", "posted": bool, "database_id", "url", "header"} か失敗の説明。一覧が読めなければ投稿しない
   399	    (既投稿かを確かめられないまま投稿すると二重になりうるため)。"""
   400	    try:
   401	        line = format_header(role, name, session_id, kind, values)
   402	    except ValueError as e:
   403	        return {"status": "error", "failure": "other", "exit_code": None, "message": str(e), "key": "header"}
   404	    listed = list_comments(issue, login)
   405	    if listed["status"] != "ok":
   406	        return listed
   407	    existing = already_posted(parse_header(line), listed["comments"])
   408	    if existing is not None:
   409	        return {"status": "ok", "posted": False, "database_id": existing["database_id"], "url": existing["url"], "header": line}
   410	    url = ids.issue_url(issue)
   411	    r = gh.run(["issue", "comment", url, "--body-file", "-"], mutation=True, stdin=f"{line}\n\n{body or ''}")
   412	    m = re.search(r"#issuecomment-([0-9]+)\s*$", r["stdout"].strip()) if r["stdout"] else None
   413	    if r["failure"] or r["exit_code"] != 0 or m is None:
   414	        return {"status": "error", "failure": r["failure"] or "other", "exit_code": r["exit_code"],
   415	                "message": r["stderr_tail"] or r["stdout"].strip() or f"終了コード {r['exit_code']}"}
   416	    return {"status": "ok", "posted": True, "database_id": int(m.group(1)), "url": r["stdout"].strip().split("\n")[-1], "header": line}

   419	# --- 報告と依頼の対応づけ ---------------------------------------------------------
   420	
   421	def match_report(request, report):
   422	    """`小さな PR の報告` (report) が、種類 `小さな PR` の `依頼` (request) に答えたものか。先頭行の待つ Issue・待つ側の宣言・
   423	    前の PR (あれば) が同じなら対応する。書いたセッションの名前と ID は比べない (名前は変わりうるため)。"""
   424	    if not request or not report or request["kind"] != "依頼" or request["values"].get("request_kind") != "小さな PR":
   425	        return False
   426	    if report["kind"] != "小さな PR の報告":
   427	        return False
   428	    a, b = request["values"], report["values"]
   429	    return (ids.same_issue(a["waiting_issue"], b["waiting_issue"]) and a["waiting_declaration"] == b["waiting_declaration"]
   430	            and a.get("previous_pr") == b.get("previous_pr"))

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.

host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

Review target: `07f60b8..6fd8276`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

Review target: `6fd8276..cd71273`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print

## If findings are fixed later

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or

findings as text.

host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
