Review target: `b68a27e..4f88e38`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

   147	def assignment_end(item, cs, asg, pr):

   178	def declaration_json(text):

   204	def results_for(cs, asg, decl_id):

   226	def declaration_stage(item, cs, asg, project_number):

   228	    持っている資源。判定の要る宣言は、着手の宣言と宣言の更新のうち、`開始可` の後の資源を外すだけの更新 (resources-removed-only) を除いたもの。

   230	    `待機` → waiting、`依頼` (宣言の書き直し) → returned、無ければ undecided)。"""
   231	    go_declaration, later, judged, prev_returned = None, [], None, False

   273	def labels_at(item, at):
   274	    """ある時点 (at) に付いていたラベル: その時点までの LabeledEvent・UnlabeledEvent を時刻の順に全部読んで求める (R24 の決まり (6))。"""

   286	def reserved_resources(item, asg, attrs_table):

   292	def resource_usage(states):

   308	def _request_done(req, cs, asg, pr_states):

    21	
    22	**判断の基準** (場面ごとの扱いを決めるときに使う):
    23	
    24	- 時刻は、コメントの投稿の時刻と Issue の出来事 (`ClosedEvent`・`ReopenedEvent`・`LabeledEvent`・`UnlabeledEvent`・`ProjectV2ItemStatusChangedEvent` など) の時刻で比べる。出来事の書き手 (`actor`) は使えない (管理のセッションと利用者は同じアカウントで書く)。Status の出来事は、この Project のもの (`project_number`) だけを見る。
    25	- ある時点の状態 (そのとき付いていたラベルなど) は、その時点までの出来事を時刻の順に全部読んで求める。最初や最新の出来事だけで決めない。
    26	- 書き手がトークンのログインと違う先頭行のコメントは、この仕組みのコメントとして扱わない ([issue-format.md](issue-format.md) の「コメント」)。
    27	- 宛先と番号を持つ種類のコメント (`開始可`・`待機`・`解放`・`依頼`) は、今の割り当ての宛先と番号のものだけを使う。前の割り当てのものは使わない。
    28	- 同じ場面に 2 つの決まりが当たるときは、利用者の変更を上書きしないほうを選ぶ。
    29	
    30	**決めたこと**:
    31	
    32	- マージされずに閉じた PR は、draft でなければ ready for review と読む (読んだ時点の `state`・`merged`・`draft` で判定するため)。
    33	- 今の割り当ての PR の候補が複数あるとき (閉じる参照の PR が今の割り当ての後に複数) は、作成が最新のものを使う。
    34	- 開いている Issue の正常な終わりの判定は、close の時点で PR が draft だった後に ready になった場合を見分けられない (PR の timeline を読まないため)。見分けが要ると分かったら、`pr observe` に PR の出来事を足す。
    35	- 管理のセッションが書いた `Blocked` は、判定の要る最新の宣言への `待機` のうち、理由に `Issue` か `小さな PR` を含み、最新の `開始可` より後の最初のものがあり、Status が `Blocked` で、`Blocked` への Status の変化の時刻がその `待機` 以後のもの。変化が `待機` より前なら利用者が付けたもの (`manager_blocked` は偽)。戻り先 (`return_status`) は `In Progress`。
    36	- JSON のコードブロックが読めない宣言も、判定の要る宣言にする (`declaration` は null で `error` に理由。管理のセッションが差し戻す)。
    37	
    38	## 宣言の段階
    39	
    40	判定の要る宣言は、着手の宣言と宣言の更新のうち、`開始可` の後の資源を外すだけの更新 (`resources-removed-only`) を除いたもの。差し戻された (宣言の書き直しの `依頼` がある) 宣言を書き直した更新は、資源を外しただけでも判定の要る宣言。差し戻された宣言は、持っている資源の計算に入れない。
    41	
    42	| 段階 (`stage`) | 条件 |
    43	| --- | --- |
    44	| null | 今の割り当ての宣言が無い (何も求めず、作業のセッションの宣言を待つ) |
    45	| `undecided` | 判定の要る最新の宣言に、判定の結果 (`開始可`・`待機`・宣言の書き直しの `依頼`) が無い |
    46	| `go` | 最新の結果が `開始可` (作業中) |
    47	| `waiting` | 最新の結果が `待機` (`wait` に理由と相手) |
    48	| `returned` | 最新の結果が宣言の書き直しの `依頼` |
    49	
    50	## 場面ごとの扱い
    51	
    52	テストで決めた扱い (テストの名前に場面を書く。`issue-dispatch/tests/test_itemstate.py`)。
    53	
    54	| 場面 | 読み方 |
    55	| --- | --- |
    56	| フィールドに ID があるが、コメント `割り当て` が無い | 割り当て中ではない (出どころはコメント) |
    57	| 前の割り当ての `解放` があり、新しい `割り当て` がある | 新しい割り当てが今の割り当て。前の `解放` は数えない |
    58	| 割り当て中の項目の Status が `Todo` にされた | 終わりでも reopen でもない。割り当て中のまま (割り当てを解除するかの問いは次の版) |
    59	| Issue が閉じていて、今の割り当ての PR がマージ済み・ready for review (開いている)・マージされずに閉じた (draft でない) | 正常な終わり (`end.kind` が `normal`) |
    60	| Issue が閉じていて、今の割り当ての PR が無い・draft | 進行中の close。割り当て中のまま (利用者の答えを待つ) |
    61	| reopen の後の割り当てで、前の割り当てのマージ済みの PR だけがある | 今の割り当ての PR は無い。進行中 |
    62	| 正常な終わりか `解放` の後に `ReopenedEvent` | `reopened` (次の版でフィールドを空にして報告する) |
    63	| 進行中の close の後の `ReopenedEvent` | 終わった後の reopen ではない (答えを待つ間の reopen) |
    64	| `PR の報告` の PR の作者がトークンのログインと違う | 無いものとし、閉じる参照の PR を使う |
    65	| `PR の報告` の PR が Issue を閉じる参照を持たない | `pr.closing` が偽 (`In review` にせず本文の追記を頼む材料) |
    66	| `待機` の理由が `利用者の答え`・`資源`・`設定` だけ | Status を変えない理由なので、Status が `Blocked` でも管理のセッションのものではない |
    67	| `待機` (理由に `Issue` か `小さな PR`) の後に `開始可` | 作業中 (`go`)。`own_blockers` は空 |
    68	| `開始可` の後の、資源を外すだけの更新 | 判定の要る宣言は `開始可` の宣言のまま。持っている資源は減る |
    69	| `開始可` の後の、ファイルを変えた更新 | 判定の要る宣言はその更新 (`undecided`)。持っている資源は `開始可` の宣言のもののまま |
    70	| 割り当ての後に利用者が足したラベルの資源 | 予約していない (`reserved` に入らない。宣言のときに空きを確かめる) |
    71	
    72	## `item state` が返す値
    73	
    74	| キー | 内容 |
    75	| --- | --- |
    76	| `key` | 項目 (`owner/repo#番号`) |
    77	| `assignment` | 今の割り当て (`to` 宛先・`number` 番号・`comment_id`・`at`)。無ければ null (以下のキーは初期値) |
    78	| `release` | 今の番号の `解放` (`comment_id`・`at`・`reason`)。無ければ null |
    79	| `pr` | 今の割り当ての PR (`url`・`source` (`report` / `reference`)・`state`・`draft`・`merged`・`closing` (Issue を閉じる参照に割り当ての Issue を含むか)・`base_ref`・`created_at`)。無ければ null |
    80	| `in_progress` | 進行中か |
    81	| `end` | 割り当ての終わり (`kind` が `released` / `normal`・`at`・`released` なら `reason`)。無ければ null |
    82	| `assigned` | 割り当て中か |
    83	| `reopened` | 終わった後の reopen (`at`)。無ければ null |
    84	| `declaration` | `judged` (判定の要る最新の宣言: `comment_id`・`at`・`kind`・`declaration` (JSON。読めなければ null)・`error`・`update_kind`)・`stage`・`go`・`wait` (`comment_id`・`at`・`reasons`)・`returned`・`manager_blocked`・`blocked_wait` (その `待機` の ID)・`return_status`・`own_blockers` (Issue の参照の配列)・`go_declaration`・`held` (名前の順) |
    85	| `reserved` | 割り当てのときに予約した資源 (名前の順) |
    86	| `problems` | 導出を続けられるが知らせるもの (`what` が `pr-unreadable`: `PR の報告` の PR が読めない) |
    87	
    88	出力の `usage` は、割り当て中の項目の `reserved` と `held` から導いた資源の使用 (資源の名前 → 持つ項目の配列。[resources.md](resources.md) の判断が読む)。
    89	
    90	## 作業のセッションの確認
    91	
    92	同じ導出の、自分の項目についての読み出し (計画の R26・R27)。書き込みの `gh` は実行しない。
    93	
    94	| サブコマンド | 返すもの |
    95	| --- | --- |
    96	| `work check` | `field_is_mine` (フィールド `Agent session ID` が自分の ID か)・`assignment`・`assigned_to_me` (今の割り当ての宛先が自分か)・`released` (今の番号の `解放`)・`pending_requests` (自分宛てで今の割り当ての番号の `依頼` のうち、まだ行っていないもの: `comment_id`・`at`・`kind`・`values`)・`third_party_edits` (`割り当て` より後の、トークンのログイン以外による本文の編集。確認の対象かは呼び出し元が決める) |
    97	| `work held` | 自分宛ての今の割り当てで割り当て中の Issue (閉じて利用者の答えを待つ Issue を含む。割り当てが終わった Issue は返さない) を Project の順に: `key`・`state`・`status`・`assignment` (番号)・`judged`・`update_kind`・`stage`・`has_go`・`has_wait`・`manager_blocked`・`pending_requests` |
    98	
    99	`依頼` を行ったかの判断: `宣言の書き直し` は、その後に `宣言の更新` があれば行った。`本文の追記` は、依頼の PR が Issue を閉じる参照にその Issue を含めば行った。`小さな PR` は、対応する `小さな PR の報告` ([issue-format.md](issue-format.md) の「報告と依頼の対応づけ」) があれば行った。
   100	
   101	## CLI
   102	
   103	| サブコマンド | 書き込み | 返すもの |
   104	| --- | --- | --- |
   105	| `item state --dir <管理ディレクトリ> [--project <owner>/<番号>] [--issue <owner/repo#番号>]` | 無し | `items` (割り当てのある項目の状態。上の表)・`usage`・`problems`・`rate_limit`・`warnings`・`errors`。設定の `project` と `resources` (属性) を読む。項目の一覧そのものが欠ければ (`problems` の `what` が `items-page`・`graphql-errors`) 導かずに `errors` (key `partial`) |
   106	| `work check --project <owner>/<番号> --issue <owner/repo#番号> [--session <ID>]` | 無し | `session`・上の表の値・`problems`・`rate_limit`・`errors`。`--session` を省けば環境変数 (`CLAUDE_CODE_HOST_SESSION_ID`、無ければ `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`)。項目が無ければ `errors` (key `issue`) |
   107	| `work held --project <owner>/<番号> [--session <ID>]` | 無し | `session`・`items` (上の表)・`problems`・`rate_limit`・`errors` |
   108	
   109	`PR の報告` の PR が読めなければ、`problems` (`what` が `report-pr`) で知らせ、その項目の `pr` は無しになる (上の表の行「今の割り当ての PR」)。

content.text: (Re-invocation of /code-review — the skill instructions were previously loaded; the arguments or dynamic output below are new.)

Review target: `5814ae0..f000bad`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

Review target: `d8704e9..3126be4`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

content.text: (Re-invocation of /code-review — the skill instructions were previously loaded; the arguments or dynamic output below are new.)

Review target: `3126be4..0091b99`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or

directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results

`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you

+
+### `wait.pid`
+
+実行中の待機の印。置き場は、管理の `wait` では記録の置き場 ([records.md](records.md))、作業の待機では `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/issue-dispatch/<セッション ID>/` ([messaging.md](messaging.md) の一時ディレクトリ。作業ツリーには何も書かない)。JSON で、`pid` (待機のプロセス)・`started_at` (そのプロセスの開始時刻。`ps -o lstart=` の文字列のまま)・`owner` (所有者のセッション ID)・`wait` (待機の名前)・`written_at` を持つ。一時名に書いてから改名する。
+
+- **起動時**: `wait.pid` があれば、その PID のプロセスの開始時刻が `started_at` と一致し、コマンドがこの CLI の待機 (`issue_dispatch.py` と待機の名前を含む) なら、SIGTERM を送って終わるのを待つ。一致しなければ (PID が別のプロセスに再利用されている)、止めずに `wait.pid` だけ消す。その後、自分の PID で `wait.pid` を書き、標準出力の最初の行に `pid <PID>` を書く。
+- **終わるとき**: `wait.pid` の PID が自分のときだけ消す (止められた待機が、後から起動した待機の `wait.pid` を消さないため)。
+- **SIGTERM を受けたとき**: 標準出力に `stopped <PID>` を書き、終了コード 6 で終わる。再入の手順は、出力に `stopped` の行があるか、`wait.pid` に通知と別の PID があるときは何もしない (止めた待機の通知で再入を繰り返さないため。計画の R24)。
+
+### 終わる条件と標準出力
+
+標準出力は、最初の行が `pid <PID>`、終わりの行が先頭の語で種類を示す 1 行 (期限と失敗の終了コードでは終わりの行を書かない)。スキルは先頭の語で分ける。
+
+| 待機 | 終わる条件 | 終わりの行 |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `wait` | スナップショットと今の Project (と `comment_prs` の PR の状態) に差分がある (「差分の種類と処理の順」) | `diff <種類,...>` (差分の種類を処理の順に、重複なく) |
+| `wait-assignment` | 新しい割り当て: `--blocked`・`--in-review`・`--pending` に渡した Issue 以外で、開いていて、自分の ID が `Agent session ID` に入り、自分宛ての最新の `割り当て` があってその番号の `解放` が無く、Status が `In Progress` の項目 (`割り当て` が無い項目は、割り当ての書き込みの途中なので返さない) | `assignment <項目>` |
+| `wait-assignment` | `--blocked` に渡した Issue が `In Progress` に戻った (フィールドが自分の ID) | `resumed <項目>` |
+| `wait-assignment` | `--pending` に渡した Issue が戻った: 開いていて、フィールドが自分の ID で、Status が `In Progress` か `Blocked` | `resumed <項目>` |
+| `wait-assignment` | `--in-review`・`--pending` に渡した Issue の正常な終わり ([flow.md](flow.md) の `end`。正常な終わりの後に reopen されてフィールドが空にされた場合を含む。進行中の Issue の close では終わらない) | `stop close` |
+| `wait-assignment` | 自分宛ての `依頼` (本文の追記) があり、その PR が開いていて、閉じる参照にまだ Issue が無い (追記が済んだ PR と閉じた PR では終わらない) | `request` |
+| `wait-decision` | 自分宛てで、`--declaration` に渡した宣言の ID を持つ `開始可` | `go` |
+| `wait-decision` | 自分宛てで、`--declaration` に渡した宣言の ID を持つ `依頼` (宣言の書き直し) | `request` |
+| `wait-decision` | 今の Issue の Status が `Blocked` で、それが管理のセッションが書いた `Blocked` ([flow.md](flow.md) の `manager_blocked`。利用者が手で付けた `Blocked` では終わらない) | `wait` |
+| `wait-decision` | `--review-update` を渡されたときの、今の Issue の正常な終わり | `stop close` |
+| どちらも | 見る Issue (`wait-assignment` では `--blocked`・`--in-review`・`--pending` に渡した Issue、`wait-decision` では `--issue`) に、自分宛てで今の割り当ての番号の `解放` がある (フィールドが自分の ID でなくなっただけでは終わらない) | `stop <理由>` (理由は `解放` の先頭行の値) |
+| どちらも | SIGTERM を受けた | `stopped <PID>` |
+
+複数が同時に当たれば、`wait-assignment` は `stop` → `request` → `resumed` → `assignment`、`wait-decision` は `stop` → `go` → `request` → `wait` の順で 1 つを返す。前の割り当て・別の宛先・別の宣言への `開始可`・`解放` では終わらない (コメントの書き手がトークンのログインと同じものだけを見る)。
+
+### 終了コード
+
+| 終了コード | 意味 | 作業のセッションの扱い (計画の KTD6) |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| 0 | 終わる条件に当たった (終わりの行あり) | 終わりの行の語で分ける |
+| 124 | 期限 (期限切れを宣言する前にもう 1 度確かめる) | 状態ごとの扱い (`available` の送り直しなど) |
+| 8 | `gh` の認証切れ | 止まり、`gh auth login` を案内する |
+| 3 | レート制限の再開 (`gh api rate_limit`) を期限内に待てない、または再開時刻を読めない (期限内なら待って続ける) | 何も送らずに起動し直す |
+| 4 | ネットワークの失敗 (接続の失敗・タイムアウト・`gh` のほかの失敗) が続けて 3 回 (間に成功があれば数え直す) | 1 回目は起動し直す。2 回目も 4 なら止まる |
+| 5 | スナップショットが無い・壊れている (`wait` だけ。書き直さない。先に `project items --write-snapshot` が要る) | — |
+| 6 | 止められた (`stopped` の行) | 何もしない |
+| 2 | 引数の誤り (`argparse`) と、間隔が期限以上 | 止まる |
+

 | サブコマンド | 書き込み | 返すもの |
@@ -88,3 +136,6 @@
 | `project items --project <owner>/<番号> --write-snapshot --dir <管理ディレクトリ>` | `snapshot.json` (GitHub には書かない) | 引数 `--write-snapshot` は `--dir` と一緒に指定する。`project items` の出力に `snapshot` (`path`・`taken_at`・`comment_prs`) を足す。項目の一覧そのものが欠ければ、スナップショットを書かずに `errors` (key `partial`) で返す。1 項目の中の欠けと読めなかった PR (`problems` の `what`: `comment-pr`) は、既存のスナップショットに引き継ぐ元があれば前の値を引き継ぎ

 | 書き込みのサブコマンドの `--snapshot-dir <管理ディレクトリ>` | `snapshot.json` | 出力に `snapshot` (`reflected`・`warnings`) を足す |

+| `wait-assignment --project <owner>/<番号> [--session <ID>] [--blocked <Issue>]... [--in-review <Issue>]... [--pending <Issue>] --interval <分> --minutes <分>` | `wait.pid` (一時ディレクトリ) | 「待機」の節。`--session` を省けば環境変数 |

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results

most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle

`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or

host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings

Review target: `28bc061..d5126eb`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

 **記録を失ったとき** (記録が無い・前の記録が `ended`): 記録にだけある情報 (割り当ての意図・問いと答え・報告済みの印・確かめた本文の編集の時刻) を失い、同じ導出で続ける。`利用者の答え` を待つ宣言は `user-answer-lost` で尋ね直し、閉じて答えを待つ項目は `close-in-progress` を尋ね直し、報告済みの印が無いので人の変更などを 1 回ずつ報告し直すことがある。確認の対象の項目は、割り当ての前に利用者に確かめ直す (U16)。どれも `record_lost` を真にして返す。
 
-**処理の順**: 項目ごとに、割り当てのある項目の場面 (`引き継ぎ` → 答えを待つ間の reopen → 終わった後の reopen と残った PR → 進行中の close → 担当者 → フィールド → Status → `待機` の続き → 第三者の本文の編集 → PR) → 割り当ての無い項目の `Blocked` の再導出、の順に導き、最後に差分からの人の変更と、Project から除かれた項目を足す。差分の種類の順 (計画の R12) は [observation.md](observation.md)。待っていた宣言の判定し直しの順 (宣言の投稿の順。同じなら Project の中の順) は U15。
+**処理の順**: 項目ごとに、割り当てのある項目の場面 (`引き継ぎ` → 答えを待つ間の reopen → 終わった後の reopen と残った PR → 進行中の close → 担当者 → フィールド → Status → `待機` の続き → 第三者の本文の編集 → PR) → 割り当ての無い項目の `Blocked` の再導出、の順に導き、最後に差分からの人の変更と、Project から除かれた項目を足す。差分の種類の順 (計画の R12) は [observation.md](observation.md)。未判定の宣言の判定の順は下の「判定」。待機していた宣言の再判定は U15 の後半。
+
+## 判定
+
+宣言の判定 (計画の R20・KTD9・KTD14・AE32・AE54)。モジュール `issue-dispatch/scripts/issue_dispatch/judge.py` (関数 `judge.judge`) と CLI の `declaration judge` がこれに従う。競合の可能性の規則は [issue-format.md](issue-format.md) の「競合の可能性」、資源の判断は [resources.md](resources.md) の契機の表、リポジトリの設定の読み方は [repositories.md](repositories.md) が正本で、ここでは言い直さない。
+
+**判定の順序と比較の相手**: 未判定の宣言 (判定の要る最新の宣言で、段階が `undecided` のもの) を、投稿の順 (同じなら Project の中の順) に 1 件ずつ判定する。比較の相手は、その時点で `開始可` になっている宣言 (項目ごとに最新の `開始可` の宣言) だけで、未判定の宣言どうしは比較しない。同じ実行で先に `開始可` にした宣言は後の宣言の相手になり、予約した資源は後の宣言には空いていない。相手の項目の PR が ready for review の後なら、PR が変更したファイルのうち相手の宣言に無いものも、節なしのファイルとして相手に加える (「PR が変えたファイルとの照合」と同じ出どころ)。比較の規則 (同じリポジトリの同じパスごと。別のリポジトリは競合しない)
+
+**1 件の判定**: 上から順に分岐し、結果 (`result`) を `go`・`wait`・`ask`・`request` のどれかに決める。
+
+| 順 | 条件 | 結果 |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| 1 | リポジトリの設定が読めない (`repo.read_repo_config` が `unreadable`) | `wait`: `待機` (理由 `設定`)。本文に理由と直し方と、直したら管理のセッションに知らせることを書く。そのリポジトリの宣言は判定しない。設定ファイルが無い (`missing`) は読めないことではなく、デフォルトの表だけで照合して進む |
+| 2 | 宣言の形の誤り (コメントの JSON を、リポジトリの規則で種類を付けて `declaration.parse` で検査する) | `request`: `依頼` (宣言の書き直し)。本文に誤りの一覧と使った規則 (リポジトリの設定とデフォルトの表か、デフォルトの表だけか) を書く |
+| 3 | 競合の可能性 (`declaration.conflictability`) の相手ごとの結果 | 相手ごとに、記録の質問の回答で扱いを決める (下の表)。ready for review の後の資源だけを変える更新 (`resources-only`) は比較しない |
+| 4 | 宣言の資源 (着手の宣言は `resources.judge_declare`、更新は `judge_update`) | [resources.md](resources.md) の契機 `declare` / `update` の行のとおり。結果 `wait` は `待機` (理由 `資源`)、`ask` は質問 `resource-busy` (対象は資源の名前) を出して回答まで `待機` (理由 `利用者の答え`)。3 で待機・質問になった宣言は 4 に進まない |
+| 5 | 割り当てで予約したのに宣言に無い資源 (着手の宣言だけ。`judge_declare` の `release`・`keep`・`ask_undeclared`・`request_rewrite`) | 同じ行のとおり。`ask_undeclared` は `開始可` を書いてから質問 `release-undeclared` (対象は資源の名前) を出す。`request_rewrite` は `依頼` (宣言の書き直し: その資源を加える) にし、`開始可` は書かない |
+| 6 | どれにも当たらない | `go`: `開始可`。本文に比較した相手の数・予約した資源・解放した資源を書く |
+
+競合の可能性の相手ごとの扱い:
+
+| 相手の結果 | 記録の質問 (種類・対象 `subject`) | 回答と扱い |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `conflict` | `conflict`・`<相手の項目>:<相手の宣言の ID>` | 回答が無ければ質問し、回答まで `待機` (理由 `利用者の答え`)。`wait`: `待機` (理由 `Issue` 相手) と、相手を `blockedBy` に追加し Status を `Blocked` にする。`small-pr`: `待機` (理由 `小さな PR` 相手。相手の `小さな PR の報告` があれば PR も) と、相手のセッションへの `依頼` (小さな PR。待つ Issue がこの項目の `依頼` が相手の項目に既にあれば出さない) と `blockedBy`・`Blocked`。`proceed`: 競合しうるまま進む |
+| `needs-user` (種類 `unknown-content` の同じパス) | `unknown-content`・`<相手の項目>:<相手の宣言の ID>:<パス>` | 回答が無ければ質問し、回答まで `待機`。`conflict`: その相手を `conflict` として上の行で扱う。`none`: 競合しない。同じ相手に `conflict` のパスもあれば `conflict` の質問だけを出す |
+
+`待機` の理由 (すべて並べる決まりは [issue-format.md](issue-format.md) の「種類」) は、未回答の質問があれば `利用者の答え` を先頭に、回答済みの相手の `Issue`・`小さな PR` を続ける。結果は、未回答の質問があれば `ask`、無ければ `wait`。質問の種類と選択肢の正本は [records.md](records.md) の問いの表。
+
+**質問の対象と書き直し**: 質問は項目・種類・対象 (`subject`) で引き、回答の無いもの (未回答・取り下げ) は回答無しに数える。記録に同じ項目・種類・対象の未回答の質問があれば質問を出し直さない (`待機` は書く)。対象を相手の宣言の ID にするのは、判定を待つ宣言が書き直されて自分の宣言の ID が変わっても、同じ相手への回答を使い、新しい相手だけ質問するため (計画の U15 の Approach 2)。小さな PR の `依頼` と `小さな PR の報告` は前の宣言の ID で対応づけたまま読み、新しい `依頼` は出さない。前の `待機` のために書いた `Blocked` と `blockedBy` は、新しい判定で `Issue`・`小さな PR` を待たなければ Status を `In Progress` に戻し、自分が足した `blockedBy` のうち
+
+**`開始可` を書く直前の比較**: 判定は常にその時点の `開始可` の宣言すべてと比較するので、利用者の回答や待機の解消の後に `開始可` を書くときも、その間に `開始可` になった宣言と比べ直すことになる (AE54)。例外は ready for review の後の資源だけを変える更新で、比較しない。
+
+**資源の使用** (`judge.usage_for`): `item state` の `usage` から、`開始可` の後に宣言に無い予約のうち解放するもの (属性 `release_undeclared` が `release`、または質問 `release-undeclared` の回答が `release`) を除く。
+
+**返すもの**: `judgments` (宣言ごと: `item`・`declaration`・`to`・`assignment`・`update_kind`・`repo_config` (読み取りの結果の `status`)・`result`・`waits` (`待機` の理由)・`compared` (比較した相手の宣言の ID)・`recompared` (ファイルの競合の可能性を比較したか)・`reserve`・`release`・`keep` (回答を待つ予約))、`actions` (「ターンで行うこと」の種類。宣言ごとにコメントを先にする (R24))、`questions` (`subject` 付き)、`signals` (作業のセッションに送る合図: `kind` が `go`・`wait`・`request`、`to`・`item`・`declaration`。`request` は `request_kind` も。送り方は U17)。`declaration judge` 自身は書かない。
+

## 判定

宣言の判定 (計画の R20・KTD9・KTD14・AE32・AE54)。モジュール `issue-dispatch/scripts/issue_dispatch/judge.py` (関数 `judge.judge`) と CLI の `declaration judge` がこれに従う。競合の可能性の規則は [issue-format.md](issue-format.md) の「競合の可能性」、資源の判断は [resources.md](resources.md) の契機の表、リポジトリの設定の読み方は [repositories.md](repositories.md) が正本で、ここでは言い直さない。

**判定の順序と比較の相手**: 未判定の宣言 (判定の要る最新の宣言で、段階が `undecided` のもの) を、投稿の順 (同じなら Project の中の順) に 1 件ずつ判定する。比較の相手は、その時点で `開始可` になっている宣言 (項目ごとに最新の `開始可` の宣言) だけで、未判定の宣言どうしは比較しない。同じ実行で先に `開始可` にした宣言は後の宣言の相手になり、予約した資源は後の宣言には空いていない。相手の項目の PR が ready for review の後なら、PR が変更したファイルのうち相手の宣言に無いものも、節なしのファイルとして相手に加える (「PR が変えたファイルとの照合」と同じ出どころ)。比較の規則 (同じリポジトリの同じパスごと。別のリポジトリは競合しない) 

**1 件の判定**: 上から順に分岐し、結果 (`result`) を `go`・`wait`・`ask`・`request` のどれかに決める。

| 順 | 条件 | 結果 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | リポジトリの設定が読めない (`repo.read_repo_config` が `unreadable`) | `wait`: `待機` (理由 `設定`)。本文に理由と直し方と、直したら管理のセッションに知らせることを書く。そのリポジトリの宣言は判定しない。設定ファイルが無い (`missing`) は読めないことではなく、デフォルトの表だけで照合して進む |
| 2 | 宣言の形の誤り (コメントの JSON を、リポジトリの規則で種類を付けて `declaration.parse` で検査する) | `request`: `依頼` (宣言の書き直し)。本文に誤りの一覧と使った規則 (リポジトリの設定とデフォルトの表か、デフォルトの表だけか) を書く |
| 3 | 競合の可能性 (`declaration.conflictability`) の相手ごとの結果 | 相手ごとに、記録の質問の回答で扱いを決める (下の表)。ready for review の後の資源だけを変える更新 (`resources-only`) は比較しない |
| 4 | 宣言の資源 (着手の宣言は `resources.judge_declare`、更新は `judge_update`) | [resources.md](resources.md) の契機 `declare` / `update` の行のとおり。結果 `wait` は `待機` (理由 `資源`)、`ask` は質問 `resource-busy` (対象は資源の名前) を出して回答まで `待機` (理由 `利用者の答え`)。3 で待機・質問になった宣言は 4 に進まない |
| 5 | 割り当てで予約したのに宣言に無い資源 (着手の宣言だけ。`judge_declare` の `release`・`keep`・`ask_undeclared`・`request_rewrite`) | 同じ行のとおり。`ask_undeclared` は `開始可` を書いてから質問 `release-undeclared` (対象は資源の名前) を出す。`request_rewrite` は `依頼` (宣言の書き直し: その資源を加える) にし、`開始可` は書かない |
| 6 | どれにも当たらない | `go`: `開始可`。本文に比較した相手の数・予約した資源・解放した資源を書く |

競合の可能性の相手ごとの扱い:

| 相手の結果 | 記録の質問 (種類・対象 `subject`) | 回答と扱い |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `conflict` | `conflict`・`<相手の項目>:<相手の宣言の ID>` | 回答が無ければ質問し、回答まで `待機` (理由 `利用者の答え`)。`wait`: `待機` (理由 `Issue` 相手) と、相手を `blockedBy` に追加し Status を `Blocked` にする。`small-pr`: `待機` (理由 `小さな PR` 相手。相手の `小さな PR の報告` があれば PR も) と、相手のセッションへの `依頼` (小さな PR。待つ Issue がこの項目の `依頼` が相手の項目に既にあれば出さない) と `blockedBy`・`Blocked`。`proceed`: 競合しうるまま進む |
| `needs-user` (種類 `unknown-content` の同じパス) | `unknown-content`・`<相手の項目>:<相手の宣言の ID>:<パス>` | 回答が無ければ質問し、回答まで `待機`。`conflict`: その相手を `conflict` として上の行で扱う。`none`: 競合しない。同じ相手に `conflict` のパスもあれば `conflict` の質問だけを出す |

`待機` の理由 (すべて並べる決まりは [issue-format.md](issue-format.md) の「種類」) は、未回答の質問があれば `利用者の答え` を先頭に、回答済みの相手の `Issue`・`小さな PR` を続ける。結果は、未回答の質問があれば `ask`、無ければ `wait`。質問の種類と選択肢の正本は [records.md](records.md) の問いの表。

**質問の対象と書き直し**: 質問は項目・種類・対象 (`subject`) で引き、回答の無いもの (未回答・取り下げ) は回答無しに数える。記録に同じ項目・種類・対象の未回答の質問があれば質問を出し直さない (`待機` は書く)。対象を相手の宣言の ID にするのは、判定を待つ宣言が書き直されて自分の宣言の ID が変わっても、同じ相手への回答を使い、新しい相手だけ質問するため (計画の U15 の Approach 2)。小さな PR の `依頼` と `小さな PR の報告` は前の宣言の ID で対応づけたまま読み、新しい `依頼` は出さない。前の `待機` のために書いた `Blocked` と `blockedBy` は、新しい判定で `Issue`・`小さな PR` を待たなければ Status を `In Progress` に戻し、自分が足した `blockedBy` のうち�

**`開始可` を書く直前の比較**: 判定は常にその時点の `開始可` の宣言すべてと比較するので、利用者の回答や待機の解消の後に `開始可` を書くときも、その間に `開始可` になった宣言と比べ直すことになる (AE54)。例外は ready for review の後の資源だけを変える更新で、比較しない。

**資源の使用** (`judge.usage_for`): `item state` の `usage` から、`開始可` の後に宣言に無い予約のうち解放するもの (属性 `release_undeclared` が `release`、または質問 `release-undeclared` の回答が `release`) を除く。

**返すもの**: `judgments` (宣言ごと: `item`・`declaration`・`to`・`assignment`・`update_kind`・`repo_config` (読み取りの結果の `status`)・`result`・`waits` (`待機` の理由)・`compared` (比較した相手の宣言の ID)・`recompared` (ファイルの競合の可能性を比較したか)・`reserve`・`release`・`keep` (回答を待つ予約))、`actions` (「ターンで行うこと」の種類。宣言ごとにコメントを先にする (R24))、`questions` (`subject` 付き)、`signals` (作業のセッションに送る合図: `kind` が `go`・`wait`・`request`、`to`・`item`・`declaration`。`request` は `request_kind` も。送り方は U17)。`declaration judge` 自身は書かない。

待機の解消 (相手の割り当ての終了・小さな PR のマージ・資源の解放・設定が読めるようになったこと・回答) の検出と再判定、質問 `small-pr-closed` は U15 の後半。

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the

altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## 契機

判断は契機ごとに 1 つの関数で、属性 (設定から) と資源の使用 (U13 が求める) と利用者の答え (記録にある。読むのは呼び出し元) を引数で受ける。利用者の答えの値: `when_busy` が `ask` の資源には `wait` (待つ) / `proceed` (進める)、`release_undeclared` が `ask` の資源には `release` (解放してよい) / `keep` (解放してはいけない)。
